meta.title: iOS parity catch-up — 2026-08
meta.purpose: Machine-readable work-list for bringing btheis15/mlr-app-ios to FULL feature parity with the web app, and beyond it where native can do better. Companion prose (the warnings, the Swift, the incident history) lives in docs/ios-parity-2026-08.md and the per-area files under docs/ios-parity-2026-08/.
meta.ios_last_sync: 2026-07-22 — the July round covered web PRs #316-#362, migrations 0114-0128
meta.product_direction: iOS is the FLAGSHIP, not a companion. Parity is the floor. A feature iOS already has is due a DEPTH AUDIT, not a tick — the web version has usually grown since.
meta.conventions: each web lib/*.ts seam maps to a Swift Services/*Service.swift; new RPCs use the Encodable param-struct + .rpc()/.from() idiom. ios_targets paths in the per-area docs are PROPOSED where the July doc didn't already name them — the iOS repo was not checked out when this was generated.
caveats: The web app is light-mode only by hard rule; iOS supports dark. Every surface here needs a dark treatment with NO web reference to copy.
Sections marked fact_checked:false did not get their verification pass — confirm identifiers before building.
Effort/priority values are the drafting agents' estimates, not measured.

how_to_use.start_with: media-token (see docs/ios-parity-2026-08.md §0) — the only BLOCKING item
how_to_use.then: work workstreams in listed order; each per-area doc holds the build detail
how_to_use.definition_of_done: the acceptance line in the per-area doc, verified on a device
how_to_use.build_check: open 'MLR App.xcodeproj', resolve SPM, Build (Cmd-B). Watch for new Swift files missing target membership. Verify light AND dark on every new surface.

skip_web_only.reason: These web PRs exist to fight the browser. iOS does not inherit any of it — a real slice of the web app's complexity is browser tax you simply won't pay.

features.name: The Family Feed itself
features.whatItDoes: Shows every post the family has shared, newest first, grouped under day headings like Today / Yesterday / Saturday, July 27, 2026.
gotchas: The web runs 8 unpaginated queries pulling the ENTIRE history on every mount and every realtime tick — do NOT port that; page posts with .range() (25-30) and fetch children with .in("post_id", pageIds).

NEVER use a PostgREST embed (.select("*, post_media(*)")) — two FKs between the tables make it return [] with HTTP 300 / PGRST201 and no error. Resolve authors/children in separate queries keyed by id.
Sort by occurred_at desc (the timeline anchor), not created_at (upload time).

Day grouping uses a LOCAL YYYY-MM-DD key — never parse a bare date string as UTC (lib/format.ts toLocalDate exists because a UTC-midnight parse once shifted every label a day early AND corrupted 10 stored rows through a picker).
Display-name fallback chain is display_name -> first word of full_name -> "Member"; diverge and the two apps show different names for the same person.
An empty feed post-0183 almost always means the account is signed in but not admin-approved — say that, never "no posts yet".

Four child tables (post_media, post_reactions, post_tags, post_comment_mentions) are NOT status-aware, so they return rows for held posts; key children off the post ids you actually received or you'll paint media from posts the viewer can't see.
features.nativeOpportunity: Real pagination + an on-disk cache + applying realtime deltas instead of refetching. The web's own workaround is a localStorage snapshot capped at the top 15 posts because of a 200KB limit.

features.name: Sharing a post (photos, video, caption, date)
features.whatItDoes: Lets a member write something, attach any number of photos and videos, tag people, optionally set the date it actually happened, and post it.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ RE-READ the created row's status and say so. The composer used to always claim "Posted — everyone can see it now" even when a trigger auto-held the post, so an auto-hold looked like a silent failure (during the 0160 blocklist regression this made ordinary posts look like posting itself was broken). p_held reflects only the client's own fail-open pre-check.
p_media jsonb keys are camelCase: path, type, thumbnail, capturedAt, capturedAtSource. A JSONEncoder with .convertToSnakeCase silently drops three of them.
Use create_post (one transaction). The old three-insert path left a LIVE half-finished post in the feed behind a "Couldn't post" error — that's why migration 0080 exists.

Upload every file FIRST and abort the create if any failed; track per-file success so a retry re-sends only failures. The old loop threw on the first bad file, orphaning already-uploaded photos and never attempting the rest.

Do NOT compress or re-encode client-side — prepareImageForUpload is a deliberate no-op now; the old canvas compression destroyed the full-res original and all EXIF (root cause of migrations 0174-0176).

Map /upload failures properly: 507 out of space, 413 too big, 429 rate limit (30/hour), 401/403 expired session, and 403 pendingApproval for an unverified member. Dropped-connection / abort / timeout are three distinct cases and the first is the most common for big video.
Moderation and video transcoding are ASYNC — status can flip to 'pending' seconds later, and a .mov->.mp4 transcode repoints storage_path, so never cache a media URL forever.
Caps are enforced by a trigger that RAISES (check_violation): 5000 chars for a post, 2000 for a comment. Pre-check client-side.
features.nativeOpportunity: Background URLSession upload — post a 400MB fest video, lock the phone, have it finish with a local notification. The mini already allows 4h timeouts and no practical size cap. Plus PHPickerViewController instead of the hidden file input that silently delivered nothing in the installed iOS PWA.
features.v1Cut: Skip the client /moderate/text pre-check (fail-open; the DB blocklist is the real gate). Skip every pre-migration degrade path — isMissingFunction, the 42703 column-group retry ladder, the multi-insert fallback.

features.name: Photo/video carousel on a post
features.whatItDoes: A post with several photos becomes a swipeable set of pages with dots and an "3/7" counter; videos play right in place.
gotchas: Render thumbnail_url, falling back to the full-res url only when it's null. This is the single biggest scroll-performance win in the app.

A video's poster frame is seeked ~10% in (not frame 0 — phone video routinely opens on a black frame). A video tile with a poster needs a ▶ badge or it's indistinguishable from a photo; a tile with inline controls carries its own affordance.
storage_path is usually a full mini URL, but branch on hasPrefix("http") — otherwise it's a legacy Supabase Storage object path in the 'post-photos' bucket.
A post with zero post_media rows but a non-nil posts.image_path renders one legacy image from that bucket. Probably zero rows in practice, but it's ~6 lines and the alternative is a blank card.
Every rendered URL — including thumbnail_url — must carry the ?t= media token.
features.nativeOpportunity: AVPlayer plus the HLS ladder the mini already builds and advertises as hlsUrl (which the web consumes not at all). Caveat: needs HLS_ENABLED=on on the mini AND a fix for signed reads, because segment URIs inside a playlist are relative and won't carry ?t=.

features.name: Full-screen photo viewer that swipes across the post
features.whatItDoes: Tapping any photo opens it full-screen and you can swipe straight through the rest of that post's photos without closing and reopening.
gotchas: The group comes from photoUrls(media), which filters type === "image" DELIBERATELY, not != "video" — a video would render as a broken frame full-screen, so swiping moves photo -> photo past it.
Wired on all four surfaces that open a viewer: post media, comment attachments, MediaGrid (work items), and both chat rooms.

The web viewer needs a <10px pointer-movement guard because a scroll-snap swipe still fires a click that would dismiss it mid-swipe — a native gesture recognizer makes that whole class of hack unnecessary.
features.nativeOpportunity: Pinch-zoom, double-tap-to-zoom, drag-to-dismiss with rubber-banding, and a matchedGeometryEffect transition from the grid tile — the Photos-app interaction the web can only approximate.

features.name: Editing a post
features.whatItDoes: The author (or an admin) can change the caption, add or remove photos and videos, add or remove tagged people, move the date, or delete it — all from one sheet.
gotchas: RLS allows UPDATE by the author OR any admin with NO time window — this is not the 24h chat rule.
Four separate write paths: posts.text/occurred_at update; delete post_media by (post_id, storage_path); insert new media at position = existing count + i; add/remove post_tags.
An edited caption re-runs the blocklist trigger and can newly hold a previously-visible post — re-read status after saving, same as the composer.
A member cannot change status by editing; moderate_content_text pins NEW.status := OLD.status for non-admins. An "un-hide by editing" attempt appears to succeed and changes nothing.
Removing media deletes the ROW, not the file — the mini's orphan-sweep quarantines unreferenced files after a 48h grace, purging 7 days later.
features.nativeOpportunity: A native date/time wheel for the backdate field instead of datetime-local, and drag-to-reorder for media positions (the web has no reorder at all).
features.v1Cut: Ship caption + delete first; media add/remove, tag editing and backdating can follow.

features.name: Deleting a post
features.whatItDoes: The author or an admin removes a post entirely, along with its photos, comments and reactions.
gotchas: Plain delete on posts; RLS allows author or admin. Cascades to post_media, post_comments (and their media/mentions), post_reactions, post_tags.
Confirm first — this is irreversible and takes family photos with it. Admin 'Remove' via set_content_status ('hidden') is the reversible alternative.

features.name: Tagging people in a post (and the "Tagged me" filter")
features.whatItDoes: Pick family members to tag on a post; their names show under the caption and they get notified, and anyone can filter the feed to just posts they're tagged in.
gotchas: This is a MEMBER PICKER writing post_tags — completely different from the free-text @mentions in comments. Don't conflate the two.
Name search rule (matchesName): empty query matches everyone; otherwise substring OR any word starting with the typed text ("b" -> all B names).
Notification kind is post_tag; a tagged member, the poster, or an admin may remove a tag.
The "Tagged me" filter is client-side over loaded posts — if iOS paginates, either query server-side or be explicit that it only covers what's loaded.

features.name: Comments on a post
features.whatItDoes: Anyone can comment under a post; the author or an admin can delete a comment.
gotchas: ⚠️ There is NO update policy on post_comments in any migration — comments cannot be edited by anyone. Don't build an editor; the write is silently rejected by RLS.
Delete is a HARD delete, not a soft-delete tombstone (that's chat only, 0023). No "comment deleted" placeholder.
There is no threading. post_reply is a NOTIFICATION kind meaning "someone else also commented", not a nested reply.
text is NOT NULL but may be the empty string for a photo-only comment — check .isEmpty, not nil.
Comments render unpaginated on web, which is the only reason the &comment= deep link can scroll to one. If iOS paginates or collapses threads, a deep link must expand/fetch the target first.
Comments are all fetched in one query ordered created_at asc and bucketed by post_id client-side.
features.nativeOpportunity: An inline "Reply" notification action writes the comment without ever opening the app.

features.name: Photos and videos on a comment
features.whatItDoes: Answering "which cabin?" with a picture, instead of having to start a whole new post.
gotchas: A comment can be photo-only — the guard is "text OR at least one file", the same rule as the post composer.
Rendered as a small wrapping row of ~96pt thumbnails (CommentMedia), NOT the full-bleed post carousel, which is too heavy for an inline list item. Tapping one opens the same swipe Lightbox.
No captured_at column on this table (unlike post_media) — send thumbnail_url only.

Uploads ride the DEFAULT category=posts, and moderation now runs in the BACKGROUND for every category — so a flagged verdict retroactively holds the comment a few seconds after it posts, via hold_comment_on_flagged_media (attach-time) or hold_content_on_media_verdict (verdict-after-row).
Write order matters: insert the comment, read back its id, then insert mentions, then media rows one at a time with an ascending position.
features.nativeOpportunity: PHPicker multi-select straight from the comment sheet, plus background upload so a comment photo finishes after the sheet is dismissed.

features.name: @mentioning someone in a comment
features.whatItDoes: Type @ and a name to tag a family member in a comment; their name renders highlighted and they get a notification that lands on that exact comment.
gotchas: Scoped to the WHOLE member list — unlike committee chat, whose mentions are scoped to that committee's roster. Don't apply the chat rule here.

Mentions are pruned on every keystroke on a WORD BOUNDARY: a mention id survives only while @Name is present and the next char is absent or non-alphanumeric (regex @Name(?![\p{L}\p{N}])). That guard exists so a member called "Jo" doesn't stay tagged off someone else's "@John".
Insertion is "@Name " with a trailing space. Autocomplete excludes yourself and caps at 6 candidates.
Rendering must sort candidate names LONGEST FIRST before matching, or "@Jo" inside "@John" highlights the wrong span.
Mention rows may only be inserted on your OWN comment (RLS).
features.nativeOpportunity: A native inline suggestion bar over the keyboard with avatars, and haptic confirmation on selection.

features.name: Emoji reactions, including who reacted
features.whatItDoes: Tap to react with one of six emoji; tap the count chip to see exactly which family members reacted with it.
gotchas: PK is (post_id, user_id) — ONE emoji per member per post. Switching is an upsert onConflict "post_id,user_id", not a second row. This is NOT the chat reaction model.
Fixed emoji set and order: 👍 ❤️ 😂 😮 😢 🎉.

⚠️ Port the optimistic machinery: the in-flight intent must live in a ref/actor (not state), because a fast second tap on the same emoji would otherwise read the stale value and re-upsert instead of deleting — the reaction sticks on. Toggles must be chained per post so they hit the server in tap order, and only the TAIL of the chain may clear the override or an earlier completion wipes a newer tap's intent.
Who-reacted names come from the already-loaded profiles map; show "You" for yourself.
Switching emoji fires no second notification — trg_notif_post_reaction is AFTER INSERT only, and an upsert's conflict path runs as an UPDATE.
features.nativeOpportunity: A long-press reaction tray with haptics, and a "❤️ React" notification action that writes the row without opening the app.

features.name: "Pending review" and "Removed" states on posts and comments
features.whatItDoes: A post held for review shows its author an amber "only you and admins can see this" note instead of vanishing without explanation; an admin-removed one is clearly marked.
gotchas: ⚠️ If iOS ignores status, every ADMIN sees held and removed posts rendered as normal posts — RLS hands non-visible rows to the author and to all admins.
Four independent ways a row gets held, all server-side: the blocklist trigger, >=2 distinct member reports, an AI media verdict at attach time, and a retroactive verdict arriving after the media row.
status may be nil in a decoded row — treat nil (and any unknown value) as 'visible' rather than crashing.
Members cannot change status; the trigger pins it. Only set_content_status (admin) and the automated holds (via the mlr.mod_bypass GUC) may write it.
media_moderation has RLS on with zero policies — querying it from iOS always returns empty. Read status off the parent row instead.

features.name: Flagging a post or comment as inappropriate
features.whatItDoes: Any member can flag something with a reason; two independent flags hide it for everyone until an admin reviews it, and it disappears for the flagger immediately.
gotchas: entity_type is 'post' or 'comment'. Reasons: Inappropriate or offensive / Sensitive - private info / Spam / Something else.
Threshold is >=2 DISTINCT reporters (deliberately conservative — one grudge can't hide content, two independent flags can). Re-reporting just updates the reason.
content_reports is admin-read-only, so the flagger's own immediate hide must be DEVICE-LOCAL (web uses localStorage 'mlr.flaggedPosts'; use UserDefaults).
Hide the Flag affordance on your own posts, and route a guest to sign-in first — reporting is tied to identity so it can't be abused anonymously.

features.name: Notifications that land on the exact comment
features.whatItDoes: Tapping "Alice commented on your post" scrolls straight to Alice's comment and flashes it, instead of dumping you at the top of a long thread.
gotchas: URLs are /posts?post=<postId> and, since 0164, /posts?post=<postId>&comment=<commentId> for post_comment / post_reply / post_mention.
Notification rows created BEFORE 0164 ran carry a post-only url — handle a missing comment param as a harmless degrade.
The web polls for the target node up to 20 x 150ms (~3s) before giving up, because the feed may still be loading. Keep that patience; a one-shot scrollTo will miss.
Two independent trackers run side by side (post- and comment-); they share no state.
If iOS paginates or collapses comments, a &comment= link must fetch/expand that comment before scrolling.
features.nativeOpportunity: Rich notification content extension showing the actual photo plus inline Reply / React actions, so the deep link is often unnecessary.

features.name: "Also add these photos to an album"
features.whatItDoes: One checkbox saves a post's photos into a shared downloadable album too, so nobody has to add them twice — and it works retroactively on an old post.
rpcs: add_drop_box_media(p_box, p_url, p_type, p_thumbnail_url, p_captured_at, p_captured_at_source, p_credit_user_id)
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ CREDIT RULE: for an already-posted photo, credit goes to the POST'S AUTHOR, not whoever ticked the checkbox — the editor passes p_credit_user_id: post.authorId. The param is honored ONLY for an admin caller, so nobody can attribute an upload to someone else. The composer's own flow (a brand-new post) deliberately omits it.
No re-upload — the album row points at the SAME mini URL, so the moderation verdict carries over.
Best-effort: a failure here must never undo the post that already saved.

For kept media there's no original file, so use post_media.captured_at when present, else the POST's own timestamp tagged source 'post'. Never label a proxy 'exif' — the mini's sweep uses captured_at_source to decide what it may overwrite.
Album options come from fetchDropBoxes filtered to !archivedAt.
The 'albums' table and posts.album_id are DEAD — the album feature is drop_boxes (0171).

features.name: Posting something back to when it happened
features.whatItDoes: "Posting late? Place it back to when it happened so it flows in with the rest" — a photo from Tuesday's lake day lands on Tuesday, not today.
gotchas: occurred_at is the feed's sort and grouping key; created_at stays as upload time. Passing null to create_post's p_occurred_at lands it as now().
Editable later by the author or an admin with no time window.
Send a full ISO8601 timestamp; never a bare date string.
features.nativeOpportunity: A native date/time wheel, and a smart default seeded from the picked photo's PHAsset.creationDate — the web makes you type it.

features.name: Jumping to a month or a day in the feed
features.whatItDoes: A Filter button reveals month chips built from the posts that exist, plus a "jump to a day" date picker.
gotchas: Month chips derive from dayKey(ts).slice(0,7) of loaded posts and only appear when more than one month is present.
Entirely client-side over the loaded set — with pagination this must either query server-side on an occurred_at range or say plainly that it only covers loaded posts.
features.nativeOpportunity: A scrubber / year-month index down the edge of the feed, the way Photos does it.
features.v1Cut: Defer entirely; it's the least-used control on the screen.

features.name: The feed staying live, and painting instantly on launch
features.whatItDoes: New posts, comments and reactions appear without pulling to refresh, and reopening the app shows the top of the feed immediately instead of a spinner.
gotchas: The web subscribes to all seven tables on one channel with event:"*" and funnels everything into a 120ms-DEBOUNCED refetch, because each refetch is ~8 queries and a burst of reactions would storm the DB. Debounce, or better, apply deltas.
Any persisted cache MUST be keyed by the real auth uid. The recorded incident: a shared cache key leaked one member's cached private content to the next user, because signOut doesn't reload the app.
Clear every cache on sign-out.
The web snapshot is deliberately trimmed to the top 15 posts plus their comments/reactions — the full history would blow its 200KB storage cap.
features.nativeOpportunity: A proper local store (SwiftData/SQLite) means no trimming, true offline reading, and delta application instead of a full refetch on every realtime tick.

features.name: Photos actually loading (signed media reads)
features.whatItDoes: Every photo and video URL needs a short-lived signed token, or the media server refuses to serve it.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ MEDIA_AUTH is currently set to 'report' instead of 'on' SPECIFICALLY because the native app cannot sign yet — enforcement would 403 every photo on the registered iOS devices. This is the gate on promoting it.

Match candidate URLs by HOST against a known set (mlr-media.duckdns.org plus the legacy Tailscale host), NEVER by prefix against one configured string — a prefix check silently un-signed every photo in the web app for hours, indistinguishable from "no token yet".

Fetch the token with no caching and treat 304 as "keep what you have", never as failure — a 304 once made the web conclude there was no token and 403 an entire album (104 consecutive unsigned requests).

Refetch on EVERY app launch, cached or not. A cached token is only a guess; if the signing key changes, the client keeps signing with a dead key for up to 24h with no self-healing — that is how a key change became an outage.
Drop the cached token a minute before expiry, and force a UI refresh when a token arrives on a launch that started without one, or URLs built during the first render stay unsigned forever.
Sign thumbnail_url too, skip anything under /assets/, and be idempotent (don't double-append ?t=).
An unapproved member gets no token and therefore no photos — that matches what the DB shows them; render an explanatory state.
features.nativeOpportunity: An AVAssetResourceLoader / URLProtocol interceptor can attach the token in one place for AVPlayer and image loading alike, instead of threading it through every view.

features.name: Sharing a post outward
features.whatItDoes: Sends a post's caption (and on iOS, the photo itself) out to Messages, Mail, or the family Facebook group.
gotchas: The web can only share title + text via navigator.share, falling back to opening the Facebook group URL with the caption copied to the clipboard.
⚠️ Do NOT share a raw media URL outward — /f reads are token-gated and members-only; a forwarded link is exactly what the signing layer exists to stop. Share the image data, not the URL.
features.nativeOpportunity: ShareLink / UIActivityViewController with the actual image attached — strictly better than the web's caption-only share.

features.name: Chat photos and videos actually load
features.whatItDoes: Signs every photo, video and file URL in a chat bubble so the media server serves it instead of refusing it.
gotchas: 🛑 MEDIA_AUTH is deliberately held at 'report' instead of 'on' ONLY because the native app cannot sign yet — 3 registered iOS devices across 2 members would lose every photo. Promote to 'on' only after this ships and report-mode's WOULD-BLOCK log is clean.
⚠️ The token rides the QUERY STRING (?t=), not a header — image loaders cannot set Authorization and a cookie would be third-party, which Safari/iOS blocks.
⚠️ The token is IDENTICAL for every member within a 24h window. That sameness is load-bearing: a per-request token changes every URL on every render and nothing would ever hit the image cache.

⚠️⚠️ Fetch /media-token with caching disabled and treat HTTP 304 as 'keep what you have', never as failure. A 304 read as failure rendered every URL unsigned and 403'd the whole app's photos (104 consecutive unsigned requests observed).
⚠️⚠️ Refetch the token on EVERY app open, cached or not. A cached token is only a guess; if the signing key rotates the client keeps signing with a dead key for up to 24h with no self-healing.

⚠️ Signing must be idempotent and skip non-mini URLs (Supabase avatars, data:, blob:, /assets/). Match on HOST, not a URL prefix — prefix matching silently un-signed every photo for hours when the env var pointed at a retired host.
⚠️ An unapproved signup (profiles.approved = false, 0181/0183) is refused a token, so they correctly get no photos — matching what the DB already shows them.
features.nativeOpportunity: Sign inside a URLSession/URLProtocol or an AsyncImage loader so no call site can forget, and hold the token in the keychain with a single refresh-on-foreground — the web version has to re-derive it synchronously during render and returns URLs unsigned when it misses.

features.name: Per-subcommittee channels inside a committee
features.whatItDoes: A committee has one room for everybody plus a separate room for each subcommittee you're on, so the Meals crew can talk without the whole committee reading it.
gotchas: ⚠️ committee_messages.area IS NULL is the committee-wide channel. Query it with .is("area", nil) — .eq with nil is not the same thing and returns the wrong set.

⚠️⚠️ committee_area_reads.area uses '' for that same channel because it is part of the primary key and cannot hold NULL. Mixing the two sentinels gives a room whose unread badge never clears, which reads as 'the app is broken'.
⚠️ Membership comes from committee_roster.linked_user_id (the source of truth since 0057), NOT committee_members. Areas are derived by stripping ' · Lead' off each roles[] entry.

⚠️ The ' · Lead' suffix has exactly one home — baseArea/isOnArea/isAreaLead/withArea/withoutArea in lib/committeeAdmin.ts. Raw string comparison already caused silent data loss on web (a lead's standing was stripped when an admin edited their areas). Port the helpers, not the compares.
⚠️ An empty room here means 'not permitted' far more often than 'no messages' — RLS filters, it does not raise.
⚠️ Select committee_roster.is_lead with a 42703 fallback if you want to keep running against a pre-0177 DB.
features.nativeOpportunity: A real Messages-style sectioned list with swipe actions per row (mute, mark read) instead of a bell button, and per-channel unread badges that can drive the app icon badge.

features.name: Private Leads chat per committee
features.whatItDoes: A room only the committee's leads can see, for the conversations leads need to have among themselves.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ There is NO admin override on this branch — a deliberate product decision. An app admin who is not a lead of that committee is not in its Leads room, so never show them the row or they tap into a permanently empty screen.

⚠️ 'Lead' means EITHER committee_roster.is_lead = true (committee-level, 0177) OR any roles[] entry ending in ' · Lead' (area lead). Both count; a committee with zero subcommittees can still have leads.

⚠️ Mirror the SQL back-off guard: if a real area literally named 'Leads' exists on that committee, the sentinel stops being magic. Web checks !myAreas.includes('Leads'). Skip it and a lead sees two Leads rows, one RLS-denied.
⚠️ area = 'Leads' is a value valid_committee_areas (0073) rejects as a role, so nobody is ever assigned it. Never offer it in an area picker.

⚠️ The gate is is_committee_lead (0177), NOT 0172's is_committee_area_lead. Read the current production definition of can_access_committee_area from 0177 — rebuilding it from an older migration is exactly how the 0160 blocklist regression happened.
⚠️ The mini's push senders already resolve Leads recipients correctly (committee-level OR area lead, with a pre-0177 fallback), so no push work is needed.
features.nativeOpportunity: Give it visibly distinct chrome (a lock glyph / different tint) so a lead never mistakes it for the full-crew room and posts leads-only content in public.

features.name: Archived chats stay readable
features.whatItDoes: When a committee or subcommittee is 'deleted', its chat history stays browsable but closed to new messages.
gotchas: ⚠️ Read-only is enforced in RLS, not just UI: the insert policy ANDs `not is_committee_area_archived(committee_id, area)`. Hide the composer or every send fails silently-looking.
⚠️ create_chat_poll raises 'This chat is archived' — hide poll creation too, and the meeting bar (web mounts MeetingSection only for a live room).
⚠️ A room is archived if the COMMITTEE has archived_at set OR that specific area does — a role can be archived out from under a still-live committee.
⚠️ A deep link may target an archived room (the notification predates the archive). Fall back to the archived list rather than stranding the user on the room list with no explanation.
⚠️ Web copy: '🗄️ This chat is archived — you can read the history, but it's closed to new messages.'
features.nativeOpportunity: Tuck them behind a collapsed section like web does, but make the read-only state obvious with a disabled input bar rather than a text line that scrolls away.

features.name: Tapback reactions that show who reacted
features.whatItDoes: Long-press a message to react, and tap a reaction pill to see the names of everyone who picked that emoji.
gotchas: ⚠️ PK is (message_id, user_id) — ONE reaction per person per message. Model it as [UUID: String] (user → emoji), not [String: Set<UUID>]. The wrong model lets one person appear under two emoji (impossible in the DB) and turns 'switch my reaction' into an insert that hits a unique violation.
⚠️ Switching emoji is an UPSERT with onConflict message_id,user_id; tapping your own emoji again is a DELETE.
⚠️ Reactor names resolve from the room roster with a 'Member' fallback and 'You' for yourself — never render a raw UUID.
⚠️ Pills sort most-used first and highlight your own emoji. The tray is 👍 ❤️ 😂 😮 😢 🎉 plus Reply / Edit / Delete.
⚠️ Verify in the iOS repo that the who-reacted expansion exists at all — reactions predate it.
features.nativeOpportunity: Native tapback overlay via contextMenu with UIImpactFeedbackGenerator on commit, and put the who-reacted list in a popover instead of expanding inline — web's inline expansion reflows the timeline and fights the scroll pin.

features.name: Replies that quote the original
features.whatItDoes: Reply to a specific message; the reply shows a tappable snippet of what it answers, and jumps to it when tapped.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ A reply quoting a soft-deleted message MUST show 'message deleted', not the original text. The row survives on purpose (so quotes resolve) — the rendering is what enforces the deletion, so a naive quote renders the deleted content and defeats it.
⚠️ reply_to_id is a self-FK with on delete set null, so an admin hard-delete just drops the quote.
⚠️ Quote preview precedence: deleted → 'message deleted'; else text; else by first media kind → Sticker / GIF / 📄 File / 🎬 Video / 📷 Photo; else 'Message'. Truncate at 60 chars.

⚠️ Web's swipe-to-reply fires past 52px with an 80px cap and cancels the long-press timer after 8px of movement. On iOS a right-swipe competes with the navigation back gesture — prefer the context menu or a very short drag.
features.nativeOpportunity: Tapping a quote can push a focused thread view or use matchedGeometry to fly the reader to the original, instead of web's scroll-and-flash.

features.name: Edit or delete your own message for 24 hours
features.whatItDoes: Fix a typo or take back a message within a day of sending it; admins can remove anything at any time, and the bubble becomes 'message deleted' for everyone.
gotchas: ⚠️ Delete is an UPDATE stamping deleted_at, never a row DELETE. Hard DELETE is admin-only (a moderation escape hatch so a client can never delete around the tombstone) — attempting it for the author's own delete makes messages look undeletable.

⚠️⚠️ The 24h window is enforced in RLS as `created_at > now() - interval '24 hours'`, but the client's Edit affordance is computed from the DEVICE clock. A skewed clock shows Edit on an old message, the UPDATE matches zero rows, and PostgREST returns SUCCESS with an empty array — the edit silently vanishes. Check the affected-row count and surface a real error; web does not, and should.
⚠️ Edit changes text + mentions only. Media is untouched, so hide the attach button while editing and allow save when text is non-empty OR the message still has media.
⚠️⚠️ Web's edit deletes and re-inserts ALL mention rows, and the after-insert trigger re-notifies everyone mentioned on every edit. Diff the set and insert only genuinely new ids.
⚠️ Stamp edited_at explicitly from the client (web does) and render ' · edited' next to the clock.
features.nativeOpportunity: Show a live countdown or grey out Edit as the window closes, computed against a server-derived clock offset, so the affordance never lies.

features.name: @mention people in the room
features.whatItDoes: Type @ to tag someone who can actually see this room; they get a notification and their name is highlighted in the message.
gotchas: 🛑 ⚠️⚠️ The committee mention INSERT policy (0024) requires the mentioned user to be in committee_members — but membership has keyed off committee_roster since 0057. So tagging a roster-linked member who has no committee_members row and is not an admin is RLS-DENIED, the web send ignores the error, and the tag silently becomes plain text with NO notification. Always check the insert error on iOS; the real fix is a migration repointing that policy at committee_roster (mirroring 0065's shape). Needs Brian.
⚠️ Candidates come from committee_roster.linked_user_id for the whole committee (not area-filtered) or profiles.house_id for a house. Exclude yourself; web caps the list at 6.
⚠️ Highlight rendering builds its regex from resolved mention names LONGEST-FIRST so '@Ann' cannot shadow '@Annette', and regex-escapes each name. Copy that ordering.
⚠️ Deleting '@Name' from the draft must drop that id from the pending mention list, or you tag someone whose name isn't in the text.
⚠️ Mention notifications use the shared chat_mention kind (default on) and are IN-APP ONLY by design — the phone buzz comes from the separate 'chat' push category, which covers every message anyway.
⚠️ house_message_mentions' insert policy is correct (profiles.house_id or admin) — only the committee side is broken.
features.nativeOpportunity: An inline mention picker driven by the local roster cache resolves instantly offline, and native attributed text makes an @name a real tappable link into the member sheet (web only highlights it).

features.name: Unread badges and marking a room read
features.whatItDoes: Each room shows how many messages you haven't seen and the last thing anyone said; opening the room clears it.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ mark_area_read's first parameter is named `cid`, NOT p_cid, and mark_house_read's is `hid`, NOT p_hid. Supabase keys RPC arguments by name — a wrong key fails at runtime as PGRST202 and looks like a missing function.
⚠️⚠️ Read rows key the committee-wide channel as area = '' while messages key it as area IS NULL. Filter reads with .eq("area", area ?? "").
⚠️ Unread count = same room filter, .neq("author_id", me), .is("deleted_at", null), and .gt("created_at", last_read_at) only when a read row exists.

⚠️ Name the FK on the author embed: profiles!author_id(display_name). A bare profiles(...) embed silently returns [] with HTTP 300 / PGRST201 when two FKs link the tables — this project has been bitten before.
⚠️ Recompute summaries when RETURNING to the room list, not only on message INSERT, or a room you just read keeps its badge until someone else posts.
⚠️ Never stamp a read row while impersonating/previewing another member — web guards on previewMode === 'off'.
⚠️ Media-only messages preview as their attachment kind ('Sticker' / '🎬 Video' / '📷 Photo'), not a bare 'Name: '.
features.nativeOpportunity: Drive the real app icon badge and a Home Screen widget from the same counts, and mark read locally-then-sync so the badge clears the instant the room opens even offline.

features.name: Mute a chat for a day, three days, a week, or indefinitely
features.whatItDoes: Silence a busy room's notifications for a chosen stretch of time, after which it un-mutes itself.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ Effectively muted = muted OR (muted_until != nil AND muted_until > now). NEVER test `muted` alone — a timed mute expires by simply going stale, with no cron clearing it, so ignoring muted_until shows the wrong bell state in both directions.

⚠️⚠️ Mute is enforced ONLY in the mac-mini push senders (they query the read tables with .or("muted.eq.true,muted_until.gt.<now>") and skip those ids), not in RLS. A local-only iOS mute keeps buzzing the phone; calling the RPC silences APNs with no other client work.
⚠️ House chat had NO mute at all before 0155 — house_reads gained both columns then. If iOS has a house mute UI it is probably fake.
⚠️ p_muted = false always clears muted_until too, so 'unmute' fully resets the row. p_muted = true with p_muted_until = nil means permanent.
⚠️ First params are cid / hid, not p_cid / p_hid.
⚠️ Web UX: bell tap on a muted room unmutes in ONE tap; on an unmuted room it opens the duration sheet (24 / 72 / 168 hours or nil). A muted room's unread badge renders grey instead of accent.
features.nativeOpportunity: Surface the mute state to the system so Focus modes and notification summaries agree with it, add the durations as swipe actions on the room row, and offer a notification action to 'Mute 1 hour' straight from a buzz.

features.name: See when someone is typing
features.whatItDoes: A small 'X is typing…' line above the keyboard while someone else is composing.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ This MUST be its own realtime broadcast channel ('typing:<roomKey>') and must never touch the message subscription — otherwise every keystroke ping wakes the message refetch path. Web separates them deliberately and says so in the code.
⚠️ Room keys are committee:<slug>:<area ?? ""> and house:<slug>.
⚠️ Configure broadcast with self: false, throttle outgoing pings to one per 2.5s, and only ping when the draft is non-empty.
⚠️ Each received typer arms a 4.5s self-clearing timer that a repeat ping resets. Tear the channel down and clear the timers on room close, or a stale typer sticks forever.
⚠️ Ephemeral by design — no table, no RPC, nothing to migrate.
features.nativeOpportunity: Nothing exotic needed, but native can drive it off the real text-input delegate rather than a debounced change handler, and animate the dots without a layout reflow.

features.name: Photos, videos and files in chat bubbles load fast
features.whatItDoes: Attachments show as small previews that open full-screen when tapped, instead of downloading the full-size original into every bubble.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ thumbnail_url EXISTS on both chat media tables (0173) and the web app neither writes nor renders it, so every web chat bubble loads the full-resolution original. /upload already returns thumbnailUrl. Writing it on send and rendering `thumbnail_url ?? storage_path` is a zero-backend-change win iOS can take outright.

⚠️⚠️ Every existing chat media row has thumbnail_url = null — an enrichment that only runs at upload time covers none of the content already there. The two chat tables need adding to media-server/thumbnail-backfill.js (mini change → PR → pull on the mini → launchctl kickstart -k). Until then, coalesce to the original.
⚠️ storage_path is a FULL URL, not a path. sticker rows hold a sticker ID (not a URL) and legacy gif rows hold a Tenor CDN URL.
⚠️ media_type is CHECK-constrained to image|video|sticker|gif|file — anything else fails the insert.
⚠️ The photo pager must filter to type == "image" specifically, NOT != "video" — chat also carries file/gif/sticker kinds and only real photos belong in a photo carousel.
⚠️ A video tile needs a ▶ badge once it shows a poster frame, or it is indistinguishable from a photo. Poster frames are seeked ~10% in, never frame 0, because phone video opens on a black frame.
⚠️ file bubbles show 📄 + file_name (nullable → fall back to 'File') and a download affordance.
⚠️ Upload target is POST /upload?category=chat&room=<slug>; chat files land under chat/<slug>/<ym>/.
features.nativeOpportunity: PHPickerViewController multi-select with HEIC/Live Photos, background URLSession upload so a big lake video keeps going after the app is backgrounded (web literally cannot), AVPlayer with PiP/AirPlay, and Quick Look for PDF/file bubbles instead of 'download and hope'.

features.name: Messages appear the instant you hit send
features.whatItDoes: Your message and its photos show up immediately, upload in the background, and come back into the composer with a clear reason if something fails.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ Upload each attachment INDEPENDENTLY. One bad file used to throw out of the loop and restore the whole draft, so resending re-uploaded the files that had already landed (orphaning the first copies on disk) and the sender was never told which attachment was the problem. On partial failure: drop the temp bubble, restore text/mentions/replyTo, and put back ONLY the failed attachments, naming them.
⚠️ Insert order matters: message row → get its id → media rows (with position: i) → mention rows. author_id must equal auth.uid(), so never let a preview/impersonation id reach it.

⚠️ Chat media moderation is ASYNCHRONOUS — /upload responds immediately and a flagged verdict lands seconds later and retroactively holds the already-posted message (0128 §5b). Never block the send on a verdict.
⚠️ Photos are re-encoded before upload; videos and files go as-is.
⚠️ Web sends on ⌘/Ctrl+Enter and inserts a newline on plain Enter, deliberately — 'too easy to send by accident'. Pick one and be consistent app-wide.
⚠️ Force the list to follow your own send to the bottom regardless of scroll position.
features.v1Cut: A plain optimistic bubble with full-draft restore on any failure is fine for v1; the per-attachment partial-failure protocol and a durable on-disk outbox can follow.
features.nativeOpportunity: A real durable outbox: persist the pending message and its file URLs, upload via background URLSession, retry on reachability, and show per-bubble sending/failed/tap-to-retry. Web's rollback is the best a tab that may be killed mid-upload can do.

features.name: Held messages disappear (and their author is told why)
features.whatItDoes: A message the safety filters flag drops out of the room for everyone else until an admin approves it — and the person who sent it can see that it's on hold instead of wondering why nobody replied.
gotchas: ⚠️ status ∈ visible|pending|hidden; the read policy returns a non-visible row ONLY to its author and to admins, so a held message silently vanishes for everyone else on the next refetch — that is the intended behavior, not a sync bug.

⚠️⚠️ Web never selects status, so the author of a held message sees a normal bubble that nobody else can see. iOS selecting status and badging it '⏳ Held for review' is a strict improvement with no backend change.

⚠️ The client CANNOT write status: moderate_content_text() pins NEW.status := OLD.status for non-admins unless the transaction-local mlr.mod_bypass GUC is set, which only the automated hold triggers do.
⚠️ Three hold paths: the text blocklist trigger (2000-char cap for chat), flagged media at attach time, and — chat's main path — the retroactive hold when an async media verdict lands.

⚠️ The blocklist matches single words as WHOLE WORDS (restored by 0160 after 0128 regressed it to substring matching and started auto-holding 'bass', 'class', 'hello' at a fishing resort). Never rebuild moderate_content_text from an older migration's body.
⚠️ set_content_status already accepts 'committee_message' / 'house_message' with p_status in ('visible','hidden'), and moderation_queue() already returns held chat.
features.nativeOpportunity: Show the hold inline on the author's own bubble with a retry/appeal affordance, and surface an admin's pending-review count as a badge — web buries both.

features.name: Report a message
features.whatItDoes: Lets a member flag an inappropriate chat message for admin review.
gotchas: 🛑 ⚠️⚠️ report_content RAISES 'Unknown content type.' for anything other than 'post' or 'comment' — chat messages CANNOT be reported today. apply_content_report() (recreated in 0128) likewise has only post/comment branches, so the ≥2-reports auto-hold would not fire either.
⚠️ docs/IOS_PARITY.md says 'add Report to the chat bubble menu (report_content)'. That instruction is WRONG as written. The web chat has no Report button precisely because of this.
⚠️ This needs a migration widening both functions to 'committee_message' / 'house_message'. Hand the SQL to Brian — prod DB changes are never applied from the app or via MCP.
⚠️ Until then, the backstops are the automated holds plus admin remove via set_content_status.
features.nativeOpportunity: Once the RPC is widened, a native long-press → Report flow with a reason picker is a few lines; the report is also a natural place to offer local hide-this-person.

features.name: Quick polls right in the conversation
features.whatItDoes: Drop a question with a few options into the chat; people tap to vote and see the results fill in live, with an option to keep it anonymous.
rpcs: create_chat_poll(p_scope, p_committee_id, p_area, p_house_id, p_question, p_options, p_allow_multiple, p_anonymous, p_allow_other, p_closes_on)
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ chat_poll_votes has NO select policy at all — deny-all RLS for every role including the voter's own session. Do not attempt to read it. Tallies come from denormalized chat_poll_options.vote_count and chat_polls.respondent_count, kept current by a trigger, and those ARE readable and realtime-able.
⚠️ chat_poll_voters returns [] unconditionally when the poll is anonymous — enforced server-side, so the card never has to trust its own anonymity check.
⚠️ fetch_chat_polls_for_room returns a SINGLE jsonb ARRAY, not a rowset. Decode the returned JSON value as [ChatPollRow].

⚠️ Polls are interleaved into the message timeline by created_at as a room-wide full-width card — NOT attached to any sender's bubble and NOT a pinned bar. The first cut was a pinned top bar and was scrapped as 'too easy to miss'.
⚠️ Any room member may create a poll (the family-polls doctrine), not just meeting organizers. create_chat_poll raises 'This chat is archived' in an archived room.
⚠️ Server rules: question ≤300 chars, 2–10 non-blank options after trimming, and an 'Other' option is appended automatically when p_allow_other (not counted against the 10).
⚠️ set_chat_poll_votes is a FULL REPLACE of the caller's votes in one call — send the whole selection, not a delta. p_other_text only matters when the is_other option id is included.
⚠️ The chat_poll_created notification's deep link carries '&poll=<id>' and NO client reads it today — the link opens the room but never highlights the poll. iOS can be first.
⚠️ Realtime covers chat_polls and chat_poll_options only; chat_poll_votes is deliberately excluded because there is nothing safe to broadcast from it.
features.v1Cut: v1 can render and vote on existing polls (read + set_chat_poll_votes) and skip the composer, multi-select, the 'Other' write-in, and the voter-avatar rows — that alone stops iOS members from being invisible in a poll the web started.
features.nativeOpportunity: Tap-to-vote with haptic confirmation and a spring-animated bar fill, plus honoring the '&poll=' deep link to scroll and highlight the poll — something no existing client does.

features.name: Answer a meeting proposal from inside the room
features.whatItDoes: When someone proposes meeting times for this committee or house, a bar at the top of the chat lets everyone mark when they're free and shows the organizer the winning slot.
gotchas: ⚠️ The bar renders NOTHING unless a meeting is live — 'live' meaning status open, else an upcoming scheduled one whose chosen slot is still in the future. It must not occupy space the rest of the time.
⚠️ Mount it only for a live (non-archived) room with a resolved scope id. Scope is {committee, committeeId, slug, area} or {house, houseId, slug}.

⚠️ CREATING a meeting is not in this bar — it lives in the room's ⋯ menu, gated on can_organize_meeting (admin, or a Lead of that committee/area; houses are admin-only). A meeting created there appears in the bar on the next realtime tick, so no cross-component wiring is needed.
⚠️ The room key for caching/channels is c:<slug>|<area> or h:<houseId>.
⚠️ This overlaps heavily with whatever the meetings section of this spec covers — build the bar as a thin embed of that work rather than duplicating the scheduler.
features.v1Cut: Omit entirely for a chat-only v1, but then note that a scheduled meeting is invisible from inside the room — a member who only ever opens chat will never see the proposal.
features.nativeOpportunity: Availability marking is a grid of taps — native gets it right with a drag-select across slots, and the confirmed meeting can be offered straight to the system calendar.

features.name: The conversation list
features.whatItDoes: One Messages-style screen listing the family feed, your house, your lead chats, each committee's full-crew room, and each of your subcommittee rooms — with last message, time, unread count and a mute bell on every row.
gotchas: ⚠️ Section order is fixed and meaningful: Family Feed, Your house, Lead chats, Full helping crew, Roles & subcommittees, then the collapsed 🗄️ Archived chats disclosure. A section renders nothing when its slice is empty — never an empty 'Lead chats' header.
⚠️ 'Full helping crew' is the renamed 'General' (area IS NULL); its row title is the bare committee name so multiple committees are distinguishable, with 'Full helping crew' as the subtitle.
⚠️ A member in no house and no committee (and with no archived rooms) should land straight in the Family Feed with no list at all.
⚠️ Realtime here watches committee_messages/house_messages INSERTs for previews, committee_roster changes for the channel list, and the member's own profiles row for a house reassignment.
⚠️ The ⋯ menu carries who's-in-this-chat, Schedule a meeting (organizers only), Email members (anyone in the room), and Create a poll (anyone in the room).
⚠️ Any on-disk cache of this list must be scoped to the real user id and wiped on sign-out — see the chat cache leak gotcha.
features.nativeOpportunity: Swipe actions per row (mute durations, mark read), a pull-to-refresh that actually reconciles, section index, and a Home Screen widget of unread-by-room.

features.name: Tapping a chat notification lands on the right message
features.whatItDoes: A mention or new-message notification opens the exact room and scrolls to the exact message being talked about.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ The SQL-built notification URLs do NOT url-encode the area, and four of the five live area names contain '&' ('Entertainment & Games', 'Art & Decorating', 'Merchandise, Fundraising & Polling', 'Logistics, Scheduling & Finance'). So '…&m=<id>&area=Art & Decorating' splits into area='Art ' plus a bogus param and the deep link strands the user on the room list. The mini's push senders DO encodeURIComponent, so the same event routes correctly via a plain chat push and incorrectly via the mention notification row.

⚠️ Parse defensively: prefer the notification's entity_type/entity_id ('committee_message' + message id) and resolve the room from the message row, or take everything after the first '&area=' as the literal area. Also worth a migration to encode it — flag to Brian.

⚠️⚠️ Web-only constraint that dictates the format: the standalone /committees/<slug>/chat route FAILS in the installed PWA with WebKit's own 'This page couldn't load' — the navigation dies before React runs, so nothing in-app can catch it. Only the Feed-embedded form works. Every notification url is therefore written as /posts?c=<slug>[&area=][&m=] or /posts?house=<slug>[&m=], and it MUST stay that way for web. iOS is free of the constraint but must treat that URL as a routing instruction to parse, not 'fix'.
⚠️ Note the parameter ORDER in the mention trigger: '&m=' comes BEFORE '&area='.

⚠️ Landing behavior: poll up to ~3s for the target message (a cold-open snapshot may only hold the last 30 messages), then center it and flash it ~2.2s. The FIRST deep link of a session snaps without animation; a second one arriving while already in the room scrolls smoothly. Re-arm on a new target — web's original bug was firing once, so a second notification tapped while already in the room did nothing.
⚠️ Chat push type is 'chat' — the firehose category covering every new message including mentions and replies. Committee push title is '<emoji> <Committee> — <area or General>'.
features.nativeOpportunity: Actionable notifications: UNTextInputNotificationAction for inline reply straight into the messages table, plus Mute-1-hour and Mark-read actions calling the same RPCs. And communication notifications (INSendMessageIntent) so a chat push shows the sender's avatar and can be routed by the user's Focus settings — a browser cannot do any of this.

features.name: The room reads like a real messages app
features.whatItDoes: Day separators, messages from the same person grouped together, a jump-to-latest pill when you've scrolled up, and no yanking you away from history when a new message arrives.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ Never hand a bare 'YYYY-MM-DD' string to a date constructor — it parses as UTC midnight and renders as the PREVIOUS day in Central. That bug labeled every fest sign-up slot a day early AND corrupted the rows written through the same picker. Use the local-date helper.
⚠️ Sender grouping collapses consecutive messages from the same author within 5 minutes (avatar and name only on the first).

⚠️ Smart auto-scroll: jump to bottom on first load; smooth-follow a new message only if already within ~80px of the bottom; otherwise show a tappable '↓ New messages' pill. Your own send always pins to bottom.
⚠️ Skip the initial jump-to-bottom when a '&m=' deep link is pending, or the room visibly jumps down and then scrolls back up — reading as an extra hop.
⚠️ Animate ENTRANCE only for messages that arrive after the first batch, keyed by stable message id, so a refetch never re-animates the whole list.
features.nativeOpportunity: A List/ScrollView with scrollPosition and native content-inset handling makes all of this far less fragile than web's visualViewport arithmetic, and the keyboard interaction comes free.

features.name: Chat opens instantly and works on bad wifi
features.whatItDoes: The room paints the last conversation immediately from the device and only fetches what's new, so it works on lake wifi and doesn't burn data.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ Do NOT copy web's refetch strategy. Every realtime event on the messages, media, reactions or mentions tables triggers a FULL re-read of the entire room (all messages + all media + all reactions + all mentions + the whole profiles table), debounced 120ms. Worse, the child-table subscriptions carry no filter — PostgREST cannot filter committee_message_media by committee — so every OTHER room's reaction wakes your room's full refetch.

⚠️ A created_at delta fetch alone is not enough: edits, soft deletes and moderation status changes are UPDATEs and will never appear in it. Pair the delta with a periodic reconcile of the visible window.

⚠️⚠️ Any on-disk chat cache MUST be keyed on the real signed-in user id, never a shared 'self'. A shared key leaked one member's cached private chat to the next person on the same device, because sign-out does not reload the page (fixed in PR #244). Wipe the cache on sign-out.

⚠️ Web persists only the last ~30 messages per room to stay under its storage cap — that limit is a browser constraint iOS does not share, but it is also why an older deep-link target may not be in the snapshot.
⚠️ Re-derive access on every open and allow it to DOWNGRADE a cached 'member' to no-access, so revoked permission never sticks.
features.nativeOpportunity: This is the single biggest thing iOS can beat: SwiftData/SQLite-backed rooms with incremental sync, a real cursor, and background refresh. Web cannot hold history at all without blowing its storage cap, and cannot avoid the full refetch.

features.name: The resort calendar (Events list)
features.whatItDoes: Shows every upcoming resort gathering — Family Fest, the 4th of July, work weekends and one-off events — newest-first with past ones tucked away.
gotchas: ⚠️ The calendar is DB rows UNION an in-code seed array (RESORT_EVENTS in lib/data.ts), merged by SLUG — a DB row with the same slug wins. iOS must ship the same seed + dedup or the 4th of July silently vanishes from the native app.

⚠️ Family Fest is deliberately NOT a DB row — it is synthesized from FAMILY_FEST so the season model has one source of truth. Creating a real events row for it produces two Family Fests with two sets of RSVPs.
⚠️ ResortEvent.persisted (true only for DB rows) gates every admin affordance, because update_event/delete_event take a uuid and a seed slug is not one. Make it non-optional in the Swift model.
⚠️ events.source gained a third value 'meeting' in 0122 — an exhaustive Swift enum without it fails decoding. Decode as String with a default case.
events read is PUBLIC (using(true)), unchanged by 0081/0183 — an empty list genuinely means no events.
Declined events (your own 'not_going') collapse into a 'Can't make it (N)' disclosure and drop off Home entirely; past events get their own collapsed group.
features.nativeOpportunity: Cache the (tiny, public-read) calendar in SwiftData so it browses fully offline at a lake with no signal; add a Home-screen widget showing the nearest event + your RSVP, which is exactly Home's spotlight card.

features.name: Going / Maybe / Can't make RSVP
features.whatItDoes: Lets you tell everyone whether you're coming to an event, and shows the running tally of who is.
gotchas: 🛠️⚠️⚠️ set_event_attendance has TWO LIVE OVERLOADS: the 4-arg p_title version (0036) notifies but never touches `confirmed`; the 3-arg version (0122, re-created after 0036 had dropped it) stamps confirmed=true but sends no notification. Web always sends p_title, so reconfirming an unconfirmed RSVP is BROKEN. iOS must send all four keys to match web; dropping p_title would silently pick the other overload and diverge. Real fix is a migration merging both, written from pg_get_functiondef — not from either migration's body.

⚠️⚠️ event_attendance read is is_approved_member() with NO own-row exception, while set_event_attendance only requires auth.uid() is not null. An unapproved signup can WRITE an RSVP and never read it back — the control appears to save then snaps back with no error. Gate the whole RSVP UI on the verified-member state.
⚠️ event_id is TEXT (uuid-as-string OR a seed slug). Parsing it as UUID silently drops Family Fest and the 4th.

Copy the optimistic pattern: per-event in-flight promise lock (a second tap awaits the first, never fires a second RPC), optimistic own-row write PLUS a separate numeric count nudge so the tally moves with the tap, and rollback + inline 'Couldn't save — try again' on error.
'Is this mine?' must resolve through the effective user id (previewAsId ?? userId), and every write must no-op while previewing.
Realtime is one 250ms-debounced channel over events + event_attendance, subscribed only by the full calendar screen; Home loads once.
features.nativeOpportunity: Actionable push: a UNNotificationCategory with Going / Maybe / Can't-make buttons lets someone RSVP straight from the lock screen — web push cannot do this. Mirror the existing haptic('success') + confetti on a FRESH going only.

features.name: Per-day RSVP for a multi-day event
features.whatItDoes: For a week-long event like Family Fest, lets you tap just the days you'll actually be there and shows how many people are around each day.
gotchas: ⚠️ The write semantics are load-bearing: 0 days selected → status 'not_going' with days nil; ALL days → status 'going' with days NIL (collapses to a plain going, no map); some days → 'going' plus a COMPLETE map with going/not_going for every day in the range. Do not 'simplify' to always sending a map.
⚠️ A 'going' row with an empty/absent days map counts on EVERY day (the whole-week default) — that is what goingByDay relies on.
⚠️ Feed goingByDay the already-day-aware summary.going list, never the raw rows, or a maybe/can't-make leaks into a day roster.
effectiveStatus() defensively re-derives the roll-up (going if the column OR any day value is going) so a drifted row still reads correctly — port it verbatim.
⚠️ hideMaybe = event.dayRsvp: a day-RSVP event drops the Maybe button entirely AND hides the maybe tally in the count chips. The question is which days, not whether.
The drill-down only appears when day_rsvp is true AND the range spans more than one day.
Guests/unverified viewers must not see per-day counts — web hides the number rather than showing 0.
features.nativeOpportunity: A native multi-date calendar selection is far better than a row of scrolling day chips, and can show each day's headcount inline.

features.name: Who's coming (event roster)
features.whatItDoes: Shows the names and faces of everyone going, maybe, or not coming — and for a week-long event, who's here on each specific day.
gotchas: ⚠️ An empty roster for a guest or unverified member means NOT PERMITTED, not 'nobody RSVP'd'. Web shows a '🔒 Sign in to see who's coming — and RSVP yourself' button instead of 'No RSVPs yet'; reproduce that or you ship a lie.

⚠️ The embedded profiles relation comes back as an OBJECT or an ARRAY depending on how PostgREST resolves the FK — handle both in init(from:) or you get intermittent typeMismatch that looks like a server change.
Guest names are masked to first-name-only via PrivateName; members see full names.

The day-filter pills (Everyone + one per day, each with its going count) are the drill-down; picking a day swaps the grouped roster for that day's going list with a 'No one's marked this day yet' empty state.
An unconfirmed row (confirmed=false, carried over from a meeting poll) gets a quiet '(hasn't confirmed)' tag plus a tooltip — visible to planners, ignorable for everyone else.

features.name: Create / edit / delete an event (admin)
features.whatItDoes: Lets an admin add a resort event with a title, emoji, dates, optional start time, location, description and the per-day RSVP option.
rpcs: create_event(p_title, p_start_date, p_end_date, p_kind, p_emoji, p_location, p_description, p_day_rsvp, p_start_time)
update_event(p_id, p_title, p_start_date, p_end_date, p_kind, p_emoji, p_location, p_description, p_day_rsvp, p_start_time)
gotchas: ⚠️ Both create_event and update_event gained a trailing p_start_time in 0101 — verify iOS passes it on BOTH, or an admin edit silently wipes an existing start time.
⚠️ Editing is only possible on a persisted DB row; the composer coerces an edited family_fest kind to 'custom' because Family Fest is not editable at all.
The day-RSVP toggle only appears when the range is genuinely multi-day, and the value written is `multiDay && dayRsvp` — never dayRsvp alone.
delete_event also purges event_attendance by event_id::text, since attendance has no FK cascade. Confirm destructively in the UI ('this removes everyone's RSVPs').
p_kind is one of family_fest|work_weekend|holiday|custom; the picker only offers the last three.
start_time comes back from Postgres `time` as a string — slice to HH:mm, it is not a Date.
features.v1Cut: Ship read + RSVP first; an admin can create events on web in the meantime.

features.name: Unconfirmed RSVPs from a date poll
features.whatItDoes: When a family date poll turns into a real event, everyone who said they were available starts out marked as coming but flagged 'hasn't confirmed' until they tap their own RSVP again.
rpcs: finalize_meeting_as_event(p_meeting, p_slot, p_kind, p_title, p_description, p_location)
gotchas: 🛠️⚠️ Reconfirming is currently BROKEN server-side: the overload the client hits never sets confirmed=true (see event-rsvp-going-maybe-cant). Build the UI, but expect the tag not to clear until the merge migration ships.
confirmed is `not null default true`, so every ordinary RSVP is true — decode as a plain Bool and only render the tag when false.
'no' voters on the winning slot get NO attendance row at all — declining one candidate slot is not declining the event.

The nudge is not a separate system: finalize auto-queues one scheduled_broadcasts row 14 days out with payload.onlyUnconfirmed, which run_scheduled_broadcasts RESTRICTS (not excludes) to people with no row or confirmed=false.
The notification deep-links to /events?open=<eventId> — that route param must be handled.
features.v1Cut: Render the '(hasn't confirmed)' tag only; skip the admin-side reminder editing.

features.name: Hiding alerts from people who can't make an event
features.whatItDoes: An admin can tie an alert or Home card to an event so anyone who already said 'can't make it' doesn't get bothered by it.
rpcs: send_broadcast_notification(p_title, p_body, p_url, p_audience, p_expires_at, p_event_id, p_exclude_not_attending)
gotchas: ⚠️ The rule is deliberately narrow: hide ONLY from an explicit 'not_going'. A no-response member still sees it, because they might still come and seeing it could nudge them to RSVP. Do not treat silence as a decline.

Two halves: client-side for live-rendered rows (Home callouts, the banner) via isHiddenForEventTarget(mine, eventId, excludeNotAttending); server-side for per-recipient inserts via the two trailing RPC params. iOS reportedly collects the target already — verify it PASSES both params, and port the client-side filter.

⚠️ event_attendance.status is always the rolled-up value (the client keeps it in sync even for day-RSVP events), which is why a plain status='not_going' check is equivalent to effectiveStatus. Do not add day-awareness to the server rule.
exclude_not_attending defaults to TRUE on both tables once an event is picked.

features.name: Scheduled reminders for an event
features.whatItDoes: An admin can queue 'remind everyone 2 hours before' or 'a day before' notifications for a specific event.
gotchas: ⚠️ Only mountable when editing an ALREADY-SAVED event — a brand-new event has no id to attach a queued row to. Save first, then reminders.

events.start_time exists solely as the offset anchor: with it you can offer hour-based offsets, without it day-based ones default to 9am, and with no anchor at all the picker falls back to an absolute date/time.

A reminder is just a scheduled_broadcasts row tagged payload.sourceType='event'/sourceId/sourceLabel, fired by pg_cron inside Postgres — it works with every app closed and the mac mini asleep. iOS sends nothing at fire time.
The same scheduler surfaces the onlyUnconfirmed checkbox whenever it has an eventId.
features.nativeOpportunity: Offer a PRIVATE per-member reminder via UNCalendarNotificationTrigger — no rows, no admin, works offline. The server cron only fires what an admin scheduled.
features.v1Cut: Skip entirely in v1; admins can queue reminders on web.

features.name: Work items planned for an event
features.whatItDoes: Shows the resort to-do items planned for a given event, so people know what work is happening that weekend.
gotchas: ⚠️ event_work_items.event_id is TEXT and NOT a FK — same reason as attendance, so seed events can be linked.
⚠️ The link table is PUBLIC read but work_items is approval + house gated, so a link row can come back with a NULL embed. Filter nulls (web does .filter(Boolean)) or you render blank rows.
sync_event_work_items REPLACES the whole set atomically and is admin-only; add_work_item_to_event is additive and open to any member.
The list renders for everyone; only admins get '+ Add'.
features.v1Cut: Read-only list in v1; skip the admin picker.

features.name: "Upcoming Up North" on Home
features.whatItDoes: Puts the nearest event on the home screen with a one-tap RSVP, plus the next couple as quiet rows.
gotchas: Family Fest is skipped here while its own season takeover spotlight is showing (planning/live/wrap) so it isn't doubled.
Events you've RSVP'd 'can't make' are filtered off Home entirely — they stay findable in the full calendar under 'Can't make it'.
The whole section renders NOTHING when there's nothing upcoming, which keeps Home lean (and on web even drives the hero-logo sizing anchor).
Home loads events once and does NOT subscribe to realtime — only the full calendar screen does.
features.nativeOpportunity: This card is a ready-made WidgetKit widget and a natural Siri/App Intent target ("am I going to the work weekend?").

features.name: "X is going to …" notification
features.whatItDoes: Optionally tells the family when someone marks themselves as going to an event.
gotchas: ⚠️ OPT-IN and deliberately NEVER backfilled — a popular event would otherwise spam the whole resort. Both the in-app and push rows must default OFF.
It fires only on a FRESH transition into 'going' (prior status is distinct from 'going'); maybe / can't-make and later edits stay silent.

⚠️ The fan-out lives inside the RPC rather than a trigger specifically because it needs the event TITLE, and a seed event has no events row to read one from — hence the p_title parameter. Dropping p_title on iOS both loses the notification and changes which overload runs.
event_rsvp IS in both mini senders' pushable sets, so no mac-mini change is needed.
Deep-links to /events (no id).

features.name: Request a cabin stay
features.whatItDoes: Lets a member ask for a room in one of the resort's cabins or houses for any dates, defaulting to Family Fest week.
rpcs: request_cabin_stay(p_cabin, p_check_in, p_check_out, p_guests, p_notes, p_for_user, p_room_ids, p_notify)
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ INCIDENT: request_cabin_stay once had TWO coexisting 7-arg overloads (0092's p_room_ids and 0108's p_notify), so p_notify was silently ignored for MONTHS and always fell back to the column default. 0115 merged them into one canonical 8-arg function. iOS MUST match the 8-arg signature exactly; verify with `select pg_get_function_identity_arguments(oid) from pg_proc where proname='request_cabin_stay'` and expect exactly ONE row.

⚠️ check_out is the DEPARTURE date and is EXCLUSIVE — nights are [check_in, check_out), nights = check_out - check_in, and the DB enforces check_out > check_in. 'All Family Fest Days' = fest start → fest end + 1 (5 nights). Off by one here silently mis-books the last night.
⚠️ cabin_bookings has NO insert/update/delete policies at all — a direct table write always fails. Every write is an RPC, by design.

⚠️ Room overlap at request time is checked against APPROVED bookings only, so two pending requests for the same room both succeed; the approval-time guard is the second line (and is currently regressed — see cabin-approve-deny-queue).
guests is INFORMATIONAL — capacity is counted in rooms, never guests. Never derive availability from it.
cabins/cabin_rooms are public-read so the place list renders for a guest; cabin_availability is revoked from anon, so a signed-out call is a permission error, not an empty result.

⚠️ Do not port lib/cabins.ts's addDays/todayISO: they do toISOString().slice(0,10) on a local-midnight Date, which returns the PREVIOUS day in any UTC-positive timezone. Use Calendar date components with an explicit TimeZone.
features.nativeOpportunity: Replace the two <input type="date"> boxes with a native two-month range picker showing per-night availability inline — the data already exists via cabin_availability and ffNights(). This is the single biggest native win in the cabins area.

features.name: Picking a specific room
features.whatItDoes: For a place broken into named rooms ("Upstairs South Room"), lets you pick exactly which spot you want instead of just a room count — so two people can tell whether they'd be sharing.
gotchas: ⚠️ A place with ZERO cabin_rooms rows keeps the ORIGINAL plain room-count flow untouched — this is additive, never a replacement. An empty cabin_room_availability result means 'no named rooms', not an error.

⚠️ A named room is an exclusive-claim unit regardless of its own `beds` count: it becomes fully unavailable the moment ANY approved booking overlaps it. beds_available therefore sums the beds of rooms that are ENTIRELY open.
⚠️ 'Need 2 beds? Pick 2 rooms' — a booking may reserve multiple rooms; cabin_booking_rooms is unique on (booking_id, room_id).

⚠️ When editing an existing booking, a room it already holds returns available=false (blocked by that very booking). Locally override it to true before rendering, or an admin can never re-save without dropping its own room.

⚠️ Closing a room or a whole place only blocks NEW picks — cabin_room_availability / request_cabin_stay / set_booking_rooms all gate on `active`, but none touch existing cabin_booking_rooms rows. No cleanup step needed or wanted.
⚠️ set_booking_rooms deletes ALL existing links unconditionally before inserting, so passing nil or [] CLEARS the assignment — it is not a no-op.

cabin_room_availability returns 6 columns since 0094 (description was added, which required a DROP first); the picker shows 'Temporarily closed' (!active) vs 'Already booked' (!available) and disables a row only when !available && !selected.

features.name: "Not sure yet" + choose your room later
features.whatItDoes: Lets someone book without picking a room yet, then come back and choose it themselves once they know.
gotchas: ⚠️ An approved booking with NO room picked still consumes capacity: cabin_availability's room-based branch subtracts one slot (0108) and one bed (0111) per approved room-less overlapping booking. Before that fix a place read '4 of 4 rooms left' with a real guest already coming.
set_booking_rooms was admin-only until 0106 widened it to the booking's own requester (user_id = auth.uid()); the overlap check is identical either way, so a member cannot double-book.
Surface 'Choose your room' only when rooms.isEmpty AND the place has named rooms AND status is pending or approved — web fetches cabin_rooms per row to decide.

The approval-confirmation email nudges an unassigned requester because cabin_booking_notification returns room_names + cabin_has_rooms (0107) — nothing for iOS to send, but the copy the member already received refers to this screen.

features.name: Approve / deny a stay request
features.whatItDoes: Whoever reviews a place sees waiting requests and approves or denies them, optionally with a note that rides along in the email.
gotchas: 🚩⚠️⚠️ REGRESSION TO VERIFY: 0092 gave review_cabin_stay a per-room capacity branch; 0104 recreated the function from the 0032 body to add p_notify and DROPPED that branch, and 0114 carried the regressed body forward. The live function only runs the cabin-wide room_count check, so two pending requests for the SAME named room can both be approved and double-book it (Red & White House has room_count 4 but 5 named rooms). Verify with `select pg_get_functiondef(oid) from pg_proc where proname='review_cabin_stay'` and look for cabin_booking_rooms. Fix is server-side; do not compensate client-side.
⚠️ Canonical signature is the 4-arg (p_booking, p_approve, p_note, p_notify) — 0104 dropped the 3-arg form.

⚠️ p_notify defaults TRUE and works by PRE-STAMPING decision_email_sent_at when false, which 'claims' the row so the mac-mini mailer's `where ... is null` finds nothing. There is no 'send email' call to make.
The gate is is_cabin_approver(cabin_id) — app admin OR that place's named approver — not is_admin.

Surface the RPC's thrown message verbatim: the capacity refusals ('% is already booked for one or more of those nights', 'No rooms left in % for one or more of those nights') are the only place a conflict is reported.
A cancelled request cannot be reviewed ('That request was cancelled').
features.nativeOpportunity: Actionable Approve / Deny buttons on the cabin_request push (once the APNs handler exists) — the person who owns a bookable private house is exactly the user for whom opening an app is the friction.

features.name: A per-place approver who isn't an app admin
features.whatItDoes: Lets the owner of a private house review requests for their own place without giving them any other admin powers, and shows them their queue on the normal member-facing stay screen.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ The admin section stays admin-gated, so the queue MUST also be mounted on the member-facing stay screen for non-admins. Web renders `{!isAdmin && <AdminCabinBookings />}` and the component computes its own canManage = isAdmin || approvesAtLeastOnePlace, rendering nothing for everyone else. Without this split a non-admin approver has literally no way to learn a request arrived.

⚠️ is_cabin_approver is the gate on review / cancel / admin_update / set_booking_rooms AND the READ RLS on cabin_bookings, cabin_booking_rooms and cabin_messages — so an empty queue for a non-approver is 'not permitted', not 'nothing waiting'.

⚠️ A named approver CANNOT edit the place or its rooms: cabins and cabin_rooms writes are direct table writes gated on profiles.is_admin only. Don't offer them that editor — the writes would just be denied.
approver_user_id null means 'all app admins review this place' — the unchanged default.
Resolve 'do I approve anything?' with one query: cabins.select('id').eq('approver_user_id', userId) — works because cabins is public-read.
An app admin sees the full queue (all places) only in the admin section, not just places they're named on.

features.name: Add a new place to stay (admin)
features.whatItDoes: Lets an admin add another bookable place — a shared cabin or a family member's private house with spare bedrooms — and name who reviews it.
rpcs: create_cabin(p_name, p_kind, p_room_count, p_bed_count, p_notes, p_approver_user_id)
gotchas: create_cabin auto-slugs server-side (slugify + a -1/-2 uniqueness loop) so the client never guesses a slug — mirroring create_committee.
⚠️ It returns a `public.cabins` composite, i.e. a SINGLE JSON object, not an array. Decode accordingly.
⚠️ kind ('cabin' | 'house') is a DISPLAY BADGE ONLY — no booking, capacity or approval behavior differs by it. The member card shows a '🏠 Private house' chip when it's 'house'.
bed_count is reused for 'extra beds outside the bedrooms' once a place has named rooms (rather than adding a column) — the label changes, the column doesn't.
cabins.notes is a free-form heads-up shown to members ('water isn't hooked up yet'); active=false pulls a place out of the bookable list without losing its booking history.
Edits are a direct table update on cabins (admin RLS), not an RPC.
