⚠️ committee_join_requests is NOT in the realtime publication, yet the web app subscribes to postgres_changes on it in TWO places. Those subscriptions can never fire. Refresh on appear / on the push arriving, not via realtime.
0 pending requests live, which is why nobody has noticed the gate bug.
features.nativeOpportunity: Actionable APNs: 0061 already retargeted the committee_join_request notification entity to the REQUEST id specifically so a sender could carry an inline Approve. Ship a UNNotificationCategory with Approve/Reject calling review_join_request from the lock screen — surface the error if the gate rejects it.
features.v1Cut: Skip entirely in v1 while the gate bug is open; web can handle the (currently zero) queue.

features.name: Add, edit and remove people on a committee; assign subcommittees; make leads
features.whatItDoes: An admin or a committee's lead adds someone (with or without an app account), edits their name/email/phone, ticks which subcommittees they're on, marks leads, and removes people.
gotchas: These are DIRECT PostgREST table writes on committee_roster, not RPCs. Two permissive policies OR together: admin FOR ALL, plus lead insert/update/delete gated on is_committee_lead_slug(committee_slug) — so a lead can manage only their OWN committee, never cross-committee.

⚠️ Do NOT use set_committee_areas for assignment: it keys on user_id and so SILENTLY SKIPS account-less roster people, which made them invisible in the roles UI. Writing committee_roster directly is what lets a Pending person be put on a subcommittee.
⚠️ Do NOT use set_committee_lead: it writes the DEAD committee_members.role column. Make a lead by setting committee_roster.is_lead or adding a ' · Lead' role.
⚠️ Preserve the roster row's OWN name on write — never overwrite it with the linked account's display name (web's RolesManager keeps `rosterName` separately for exactly this).
A role can have MORE THAN ONE lead. Don't build a single-lead picker.
(committee_slug, name) is UNIQUE — a duplicate name fails 23505. Surface it.
Adding an email'd account-less person auto-creates a family_roster row (0125 trigger), so the admin can manage their house/phone/invite in one place. Say so in the UI.
Offer the pending-people picker from family_roster (fetchPendingRosterPeople) — it's the superset, and includes family who aren't on any committee yet.
Removing a person = deleting the roster row, which revokes their chat access. Confirm destructively.
features.nativeOpportunity: CNContactPicker for the add flow — name, email and phone in one tap, with the email correct. Also a native multi-select for area assignment instead of a wrap of tap-toggle chips.
features.v1Cut: v1: read-only roster. Defer add/edit/remove and lead toggles to v2 — an admin can use the web app.

features.name: Committee-level leads (a lead with no subcommittee)
features.whatItDoes: A committee can name as many overall leads as it likes without needing any subcommittees at all — they get the private Leads chat and can run the roster.
gotchas: is_lead is boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false. 0 rows use it live, so you have no real data to look at — set one in a test.

⚠️ Unify the two notions in ONE client helper: isCommitteeLead = r.isLead || r.roles.contains { $0.hasSuffix(' · Lead') }. Anything that checks only one of the two will be wrong for one of the two committees.

⚠️ is_committee_lead deliberately EXCLUDES app admins (an admin who isn't a lead is not in the Leads room). Don't 'helpfully' add an admin bypass client-side — but see join-request-queue for where that same omission is a bug.

⚠️ An account-less lead grants NOTHING: Keith Thibodeau holds 'Entertainment & Games · Lead' with linked_user_id NULL, so he shows a Lead badge and is a mailto target but can never satisfy is_committee_lead (which needs linked_user_id = auth.uid()). Of 5 lead entries live, only 4 confer anything. Gate affordances on the LINKED entry.
Don't call the older is_committee_area_lead / is_committee_area_lead_slug — nothing live references them and they miss committee-level leads.

features.name: The private "Leads" chat entry point
features.whatItDoes: Every committee has a side room only its leads can see, for discussing and deciding without the whole committee watching.
gotchas: No new tables: it's the reserved string area = 'Leads' on committee_messages, so unread/mute/mark-read all work unchanged through the existing RPCs.

⚠️ Mirror the SQL's not-exists guard client-side: skip the Leads channel row if a REAL committee_areas row named 'leads' exists (0 do today), because the DB branch backs off to ordinary-area behaviour in that case and the sentinel would otherwise hijack a real role.
⚠️ No admin override, on purpose. An app admin who isn't a lead of that committee must NOT see the room.
⚠️ 'Leads' is not a valid area for assignment — valid_committee_areas would reject it — so nobody is ever assigned it and it will never appear in an area picker.

Web opens every committee room through the Feed (/posts?c=&area=) because the standalone /committees/<slug>/chat route dies in the installed PWA before React runs. That's a WebKit-container bug with NO iOS equivalent — don't copy the URL shape as if it were meaningful.

features.name: Create, rename and delete committees
features.whatItDoes: An app admin makes a new committee, edits its name/emoji/description, archives it (reversibly), restores it, or deletes it forever.
gotchas: ⚠️ The SLUG IS IMMUTABLE. update_committee edits display fields only, because committee_roster and committee_areas key off the slug with NO foreign key — changing it orphans both tables. Never expose a slug editor.
create_committee RETURNS the new committees row (auto-slugged via slugify with -1/-2 de-duping); the others return void.
Arg names are exact and Supabase keys by name: it's `cid`, not `p_cid`, on every RPC except create_committee.
update_committee coalesces each param to the existing value when blank/null — so you can send only what changed.
'Delete' in the UI must mean ARCHIVE with restore-is-easy copy; 0178's delete_committee is a separate 'Delete forever' offered only on already-archived items, and it cascades away all chat history.
committee_roster/committee_areas have no FK to committees, so delete_committee removes them explicitly before the cascade. Don't try to clean up client-side.
features.v1Cut: Omit entirely in v1 — 2 committees change a few times a year and an admin can use the web app.

features.name: Create, describe, rename and delete subcommittees (roles)
features.whatItDoes: An admin adds a subcommittee to a committee, gives it a description, renames it, archives it, or deletes it forever — and each one is its own chat channel.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ rename_committee_area IS NOT A TABLE EDIT — it is a SEVEN-WAY cascade in one transaction: committee_areas, committee_roster.roles[] (both 'X' and 'X · Lead'), committee_members.areas[] (both forms), committee_messages.area (the CHAT HISTORY), committee_area_reads.area, committee_join_requests.requested_areas[]/requested_area, and meetings.area (added by 0121 because 0112 predated meetings and a rename orphaned the scheduled meeting). Renaming by writing the table strips history and memberships off the old name.

⚠️⚠️ THE 0170 INCIDENT: committee_areas had RLS ENABLED WITH ZERO POLICIES (switched on out-of-band from the Supabase dashboard, almost certainly to silence the Security Advisor). Writes kept working because the RPCs are SECURITY DEFINER; READS returned zero rows WITH NO ERROR because RLS filters, it doesn't raise. Adding a subcommittee looked like it did nothing, every time. And the seed fallback made Family Fest look healthy, so it went unnoticed for months.

⚠️ Knock-on from that: the role picker only renders when areaOptions.length > 0, so the ASSIGNMENT UI didn't exist on screen either — one unreadable table silently deleted the whole feature in both directions. When a list reads empty but writes succeed, check pg_policies FIRST.
⚠️ In Swift, never merge empty/denied/failed: `enum Load<T> { case loaded(T), empty, denied, failed(Error) }`. PostgREST returns 200 + [] for an RLS-denied read.
⚠️ Ship NO hardcoded area seed. Web's FAMILY_FEST_AREAS says 'Meals' where the DB says 'Meals & Head Chefs', and its fallback fires on ANY read error, not just a missing table.
Validation rejects empty names, 'general'/'General' (reserved for area IS NULL), and anything already ending ' · Lead'. Surface the thrown message inline.
Re-adding an archived name UN-ARCHIVES it (history returns live) instead of erroring on the PK — say so in the UI.
Archiving deliberately does NOT strip the role from anyone's roles[]; that's what preserves 'they were in it' and makes restore a flag flip.
delete_committee_area is destructive: it array_removes both forms from every roster/members list AND deletes that channel's committee_messages and committee_area_reads.
features.v1Cut: v1: read committee_areas from the DB (non-negotiable) but omit the whole editor. Adding a description is the cheapest single piece to add later.

features.name: Archived committees & subcommittees (read-only history)
features.whatItDoes: A committee or subcommittee that's been retired drops out of the live lists but its chat history stays readable, tucked away, and it can be brought back exactly as it was.
gotchas: Read-only is enforced in RLS, not just UI: the committee_messages insert policy carries AND NOT is_committee_area_archived(committee_id, area). Render with NO composer rather than relying on the insert failing.
A channel is archived if its COMMITTEE is archived OR its ROLE's committee_areas row is archived — build the set from both archived_at columns.
Reads still work for the people who were in it plus admins; that's deliberate and is what makes the history readable.
Keep archived chats reachable even for a member who has ONLY archived chats.
Confirm-dialog copy must say archive / restorable, not permanently delete — the destroy path is a separate action on already-archived items.
features.v1Cut: Omit the archived disclosure in v1; there are 0 archived committees and 0 archived areas live.

features.name: Family roster — relatives who aren't on the app yet
features.whatItDoes: Keeps the whole family's names, emails and phone numbers on file with a house assignment, so they still get every house and resort email, and everything pre-set for them switches on the moment they sign up.
gotchas: 14 rows live, 12 unlinked. Read = is_approved_member(); write = app admins only. An unverified account reads ZERO rows — show the verification state, not an empty list.
⚠️ UNIQUE index on lower(email) WHERE email IS NOT NULL — a second row with the same address fails 23505. Surface it.
⚠️ You cannot set linked_user_id yourself: link_family_roster_from_row() nulls it and re-derives from the email. Email is the only key.

One signup fires three things at once: the link stamp, the pre-assigned house applied to profiles.house_id (ONLY when it's null, so it never overrides a later explicit assignment), and the temp name seeding display_name (only when the member's own is blank or the raw email prefix, e.g. 'motu42').
Applying the house is NOT an escalation: house_id is out of the client update allowlist entirely, so this is just the admin's earlier decision taking effect.

⚠️ Two cascade triggers (0125) keep the rosters from drifting: adding an email'd account-less person to ANY committee auto-creates a family_roster row; editing name/email/phone here cascades to their account-less committee slots, matched by the OLD email, keeping the slot's old name on a (committee_slug, name) collision. Both are INSERT/UPDATE-only — deleting a family_roster row never touches committee slots or real accounts.

⚠️⚠️ 0184's lesson: 0183 tightened 29 RLS POLICIES but contained no function statements, and a SECURITY DEFINER function bypasses RLS by design — so directory_recipients() and admin_recipients() kept their old 'any signed-in user' check and leaked the whole 68-person family email directory (12 of whom never made an account) plus all 7 admins to any throwaway signup over the public RPC endpoint. If you add an RPC here, put the predicate INSIDE the body, and re-run 0184's pg_proc audit query.
⚠️ PostgREST embed ambiguity again: family_roster has TWO FKs to profiles (linked_user_id, updated_by) — name the FK, `profiles:linked_user_id(...)`.
family_roster is NOT in the realtime publication.
features.nativeOpportunity: CNContactPicker makes bulk-entering 12 relatives (name + email + phone) a few taps instead of 36 typed fields — and the email, the only field that makes linking work at all, comes out correct.
features.v1Cut: v1: read-only list of who's on the roster and whether they're on the app yet. Defer add/edit/remove, house chips and Invite/Invite-all.

features.name: Email a whole committee, its leads, or one subcommittee
features.whatItDoes: One tap drafts an email to everyone on a committee, to just the people running it, or to just one subcommittee — including relatives who don't have an account.
gotchas: Nothing is sent from the app — it's a hand-off. Web builds `mailto:?bcc=…`; on iOS use MFMailComposeViewController.

⚠️ committee_member_recipients(cid) returns a trailing roles text[] (0124) but reads the LEGACY committee_members.areas, so roles is empty for anyone seeded straight into the roster (most people). Resolve recipients from committee_roster yourself for a committee/role blast; keep the RPC for the shared composer.

Resolve each person's address the same way the roster does: the linked profile's contact_email wins, then their login email, then the roster row's own email — so account-less people are included and nobody's stale address is used.
'Email the leads' means everyone with is_lead OR any ' · Lead' role — including account-less ones, who are legitimate mailto targets even though they can't satisfy is_committee_lead.
Web warns past MAILTO_WARN_COUNT = 50 recipients because mail apps truncate or refuse a long mailto: URL — a native compose sheet has no such cliff, so drop the warning.
All these RPCs are SECURITY DEFINER; after 0184 the two directory ones require an APPROVED member, so an unverified account gets nothing.
features.nativeOpportunity: MFMailComposeViewController removes the mailto URL-length cliff entirely, and the roster row can carry real Call/Message/Mail swipe actions instead of a row of tiny link glyphs.
features.v1Cut: Ship 'Email everyone' and 'Email the leads' only; defer per-role and the shared composer pools.

features.name: The Family Fest season (off-season → planning → live → wrap)
features.whatItDoes: The whole app quietly changes shape across the year: a quiet banner most months, a 'planning underway' phase from 60 days out, a full 'Day 3 of 7' takeover during the week, and a 'post your photos' tail for two weeks after.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ MUST be computed from a live 'now'. A build-time evaluation freezes the phase at ship; a launch-once evaluation freezes it for as long as the app stays resident — which during fest week is days, so a backgrounded app shows 'Day 1 of 7' on Friday.
Recompute on willEnterForeground, NSCalendarDayChanged, significantTimeChange, a next-midnight timer, and any fest_config date change.
Use Calendar.startOfDay + dateComponents(.day), never TimeInterval/86400 — DST breaks the raw division and can flip a rounding boundary.

⚠️ fest_config (2026-07-27→2026-07-31) and the lib/data.ts FAMILY_FEST constant (2026-07-26→2026-08-01) ALREADY DISAGREE on web. Read fest_config and only fest_config; bundle a constant strictly as the offline seed.
Exact constants: PLANNING_LEAD_DAYS = 60, WRAP_TAIL_DAYS = 14. isSoon = isPlanning && daysUntilStart <= 7.
Publish it as an ObservableObject seeded synchronously, so no view flashes an off-season banner during the live week.
features.nativeOpportunity: A phase transition can drive real system integration a browser cannot: start a Live Activity when phase flips to live, end it at wrap; swap to a fest app-icon alternate; schedule the widget timeline.

features.name: Family Fest hub screen
features.whatItDoes: The one screen that answers 'what is Family Fest and what's happening' — cover photo, name, theme and dates, then today, RSVP, dues, committee contact, and the whole week.
gotchas: Order is deliberate: cover → title/theme/dates → Edit pill → FestStatus → FestRsvp → dues callout → committee link → FestWeek.
Sub-nav is Overview · Dinners · Pay only. There is deliberately NO Schedule pill — the Overview already renders the full week, so a Schedule tab showed the same accordion twice.
⚠️ The theme string 'Ye Olde Family Feste' lives ONLY in lib/data.ts — there is no theme column in fest_config. Bundle it or ask for a column.
⚠️ can_edit_fest() must be cached/seeded (web persists it under canEditFest.{uid}) or the Edit pill pops in a frame or two late on every visit.
Hide the sub-nav on the editor surfaces (planner/master) — they carry their own chrome.
features.nativeOpportunity: Render entirely from an on-disk cache with a quiet 'as of 8:12 AM' line instead of a spinner — this screen is opened dozens of times a day on weak lake wifi.

features.name: "Happening today" (Day n of N)
features.whatItDoes: During the week, the top of the fest screen shows every event today plus tonight's dinner in full — time, place, what it is, what to bring, and who to call — so nobody has to dig on the day.
gotchas: Events and the dinner merge into ONE time-ordered timeline via dayTimeline() — a 5:30 dinner sorts before a 6:30 event, not pinned to the bottom of the day.
Unset/unparseable times sort last (+Infinity), stably, so ties keep events before the dinner.
⚠️ Filter out anytime events from 'today' (eventsForDay(...).filter(e => !e.anytime)) or the scavenger hunt appears on all seven days.
Cards are fully expanded — no tap-to-expand here, unlike FestWeek's rows.
⚠️ Countdown: at diff == 0 swap to '🎉 Family Fest is on'; before the first tick show '——' placeholders, never a fake '00'.
⚠️ Wrap CTA points at the Drop Box album (FEST_ALBUM_BOX_ID = 0000fe57-2026-4000-8000-000000000001), which iOS does not have yet — don't ship a dead link.
Empty state is 'Nothing scheduled today — enjoy the lake! 🛶', shown only when there are no events AND no dinner.
features.nativeOpportunity: This is the screen that deserves a Live Activity and a widget: 'Day 3 of 7 · next: Dinner 6:00 PM · Main Lodge', updated off the same timeline. Plus MapKit on the location line and a contact sheet instead of a bare tel: hop.

features.name: The whole week (day-by-day schedule)
features.whatItDoes: Every day of the fest as a card, each event and that night's dinner expanding in place to its full detail — no drilling into separate pages.
gotchas: Day cards come from days-that-have-content (a Set over event days + dinner days, sorted) — NOT the full config window. The full window (eventDays) is a separate list used only for the editors' day pickers. Keep them distinct.
⚠️ Today STAYS in the list during the live week. It used to be omitted 'because FestStatus covers it', which removed today's row AND its edit button.
⚠️ Mount a tournament/realtime-bearing subview only while the row is expanded — otherwise you open one channel per event row across seven days.
Dinner rows show a 2-up Served / Crew-preps tile grid; prep location falls back to the served location when null.
⚠️ 'links' is the 0142 jsonb array. link_url/link_label were DROPPED — naming them in a select fails the whole request.
features.nativeOpportunity: A native List with sticky day headers and swipe actions (call the lead, add to calendar, share) beats an accordion; and the whole week can be persisted for offline reading.

features.name: "Anytime all week" things to do
features.whatItDoes: Things with no set time — the scavenger hunt, merch pickup — listed in their own group instead of pinned to a day.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ iOS STILL READS fest_activities. That table only still exists because of iOS, and a web edit to a converted event does not reflect on the untouched activity row — the two are drifting in live data right now. Switch iOS to fest_schedule_items where anytime = true; that is what finally lets the table be dropped.
⚠️ An anytime item still has a NOT NULL day, parked on current_date by 0141. Never display or group on it.
0141 folded the old blurb + details into the event's single description with concat_ws(E'\n\n', …) — a two-field iOS layout becomes one body field.
Use source_activity_id / source_activity_slot_id / source_activity_signup_id to reconcile any iOS-local state; the conversion is idempotent.

formatEventTime has THREE distinct strings: 'TBD' (day-locked, time still pending), 'No specific time' (anytime, no slots), 'Specific time slots' (anytime with non-headcount sign-ups). Port all three — they mean different things.

features.name: Single event detail screen
features.whatItDoes: One event on its own screen — what it is, where, what to bring, who's in charge, its sign-ups and tournament. The target of notification and call-out deep links.
gotchas: This is the deep-link target: /family-fest/schedule/{id} is what a Home call-out's 'Sign up' button and every change-notify notification point at. iOS needs a matching route in its deep-link handler or those taps land nowhere.
Header reads 'Anytime all week' instead of a date when anytime is true.
A missing event must say 'This event isn't on the schedule anymore' — not 404 hard, since a DB-only event may not have resolved yet.
canManage here is the same predicate as everywhere: can_edit_fest() OR leadUserId == uid OR crewUserIds contains uid.
⚠️ This screen has NO edit affordance on web (a known pre-existing gap — the dinner equivalent does). Don't assume symmetry.
features.nativeOpportunity: Universal Links so a notification tap opens the native event screen rather than Safari, and a share sheet that exports the event as a calendar invite.

features.name: Dinners — the weekly menu
features.whatItDoes: Reads like a menu posted on the fridge: each night's day, serving time, what's being made, the head chef, and which families are on crew — all visible at once, no tapping.
gotchas: No tap-to-expand and no click-through by design — everything a reader needs is on the card.
⚠️ Deliberately OMITS crew prep time/location. Only the crew needs that logistics; it stays editable but is not shown to every reader. Don't 'complete' the card by adding it back.
Edit is an always-visible button (not hidden behind a tap), opening the chef/crew narrow sheet or the full DinnerSheet depending on permission.
'houses' is family names as free text (comma-split on save), NOT member ids. crew_user_ids is the separate who-can-edit list.
Render chef_name (the trigger-synced snapshot), not a name resolved from profiles — an account-less chef's name exists only in that column.
The standalone dinners/[id] detail route still exists for direct links but nothing in the app points at it; keep or drop deliberately.
features.nativeOpportunity: A chef can attach a photo of the dish straight from the camera; the menu text supports Dynamic Type properly for older eyes, which the web only approximates with a text-size control.

features.name: Chef/lead/crew self-edit of operational details
features.whatItDoes: Whoever is actually cooking that night or running that event can fix the menu, the time, or the location themselves — without being on the Family Fest committee.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ The narrowness is CLIENT-SIDE ONLY. Postgres RLS is row-level, not column-level — the 0099/0110 FOR UPDATE policies authorize the whole ROW, so a lead or crew member with a REST client can change day/title/lead_user_id/crew_user_ids. NEVER show the full editor to someone whose can_edit_fest() is false. Actually enforcing it needs a SECURITY DEFINER RPC per surface (a real migration — raise it, don't ship it unilaterally).

⚠️ Writes MUST be partial (a small dictionary PATCH), not a full-model encode. The web comment: updateDinnerDetails deliberately avoids saveDinner 'which always writes every DinnerInput field and would clobber fields this surface never touches, e.g. position'. A full-model save from a screen that never loaded position writes 0 and reorders the schedule.
Dinner scope is exactly {menu, served_time, served_location, prep_time, prep_location}. Event scope is exactly {location, description, bring, links}.
The policies are FOR UPDATE, not FOR ALL — a chef cannot insert or delete a dinner.
⚠️ Don't copy the web's nil→'TBD' coercion into the model layer: the edit sheet then has to undo it (menu === 'TBD' ? '' : menu), which silently blanks a chef who literally types 'TBD'.
The edit permission check uses *_user_id, never a name match.
features.nativeOpportunity: A chef standing in the kitchen with no signal can edit and have it queue: an offline write queue that retries on reconnect is exactly the case a browser form cannot handle.

features.name: Full committee editing, right where the item shows
features.whatItDoes: An admin or committee member can change an event's or dinner's day, title, time, chef, crew and houses from the schedule itself — no trip to the Planner.
gotchas: Web reuses the Planner's OWN ScheduleSheet/DinnerSheet (exported for exactly this) rather than a duplicate narrower form. Do the same on iOS — one editor, two entry points.

⚠️ Only fetch the draft rows + member directory once can_edit_fest() resolves TRUE. Three extra round-trips on the busiest screen of the year otherwise; a chef/crew self-editor or ordinary member must never pay for them.
The full editor needs the DRAFT row (position, is_private, lead links), which the display model deliberately drops — you need a second, wider fetch/model.
fullEdit = canEditAll && draft != nil. If the draft hasn't landed, fall back to the narrow sheet rather than showing a broken full form.
After a save, both the content bundle and the drafts must reload (web threads an onContentSaved callback up to the screen that owns the fetch).
features.v1Cut: Ship the narrow self-edit sheets first and keep sending full editors to the web master editor via the existing session hand-off. Full in-place editing is the largest read-path-adjacent chunk in this section.

features.name: Lead/chef names that follow a rename
features.whatItDoes: When someone changes their display name, every event they lead and dinner they cook updates to the new name automatically.
gotchas: Fully server-side — a profiles AFTER UPDATE OF display_name trigger plus a one-time backfill. It fixed web and iOS at once precisely because both read the same columns. NO client change is needed.
⚠️ Therefore: RENDER lead_name / chef_name, not a name you join from profiles. An account-less lead's name exists ONLY in the snapshot column, so a join diverges from web and shows nothing.
Use *_user_id ONLY for the 'is this me?' edit check — never a name match. The trigger itself matches on *_user_id for the same reason (an account-less lead is left untouched).
An empty/blank lead_name means 'no lead' (render no In-charge block), not 'unknown lead'. Dinners differ: a missing chef coerces to 'TBD' so the card always has a chef line.
The bug this fixed: a member assigned while their name was still the email prefix 'motu42' kept showing motu42 forever, even though the edit sheet resolved the live profile.

features.name: Dues calculator
features.whatItDoes: Plus/minus steppers per dues tier — '2 adults, 1 kid' — that work out the total and fill in the payment amount and note for you.
gotchas: Two groups: flat tiers (count × amount) and per_day tiers (count × amount × days), where ALL per-day tiers share ONE day-count stepper — a single payment assumes everyone in it is here the same span. Mixed households run it twice; Reset clears it.
maxDays = max(1, getFestSeason(config.startDate, config.endDate).totalDays) — another reason the season function has to be right.
⚠️ amount is a nullable INT of whole dollars. nil means TBD — never render '$0', and render NO stepper at all for an unpriced tier.
The per-day block only appears when at least one per_day tier has a non-nil amount.
Counts clamp to 0…99.
Generated note format: '{label} — 2 Adult (high school & up); 3 days: 1 Per day'. title/noteLabel are props so a non-fest dues screen can reuse it.
features.nativeOpportunity: Steppers with real haptics and .contentTransition(.numericText()) on the running total; the total can be handed straight to the native Venmo app rather than a browser bounce.

features.name: Pay screen
features.whatItDoes: Who to pay for the week and how — a Venmo button pre-filled with the amount and note, a PayPal link, and copyable Zelle / Apple Cash handles.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ fest_payees is PUBLIC-READ at the DB level. The privacy is a client-side sign-in wall ONLY — iOS must implement its own gate or every payment handle ships to anonymous clients.
Amount and Note are parent-controlled specifically so the dues calculator can drive them; typing directly must still work.
Venmo URL: https://venmo.com/{handle}?txn=pay&amount=&note= (URL-encoded, handle without a leading @).
PayPal: paypal.me/{handle}[/{amount}] ONLY when the handle isn't an email — there is no pay-by-email deep link, so an email handle becomes a copy row instead.
No payment credentials live in the app; every path hands off to the user's own payment app.
Brand colors are tokenized (--color-venmo #3d95ce, --color-paypal #003087) — don't hard-code.
features.nativeOpportunity: Open the installed Venmo/PayPal app via its URL scheme with the https URL as universal-link fallback; add a UIMenu Copy/Share on each handle; render the Venmo QR on-device (never via a third-party QR API) the way MemberSheet already does on web.

features.name: Family Fest Planner (the editor)
features.whatItDoes: Where organizers build the week: add and edit events, dinners, dues tiers, payees, the cover image, and the fest name and dates.
gotchas: ⚠️ There are NO write RPCs. Fest content is written by DIRECT table insert/update/delete under RLS — unusual for this codebase, so don't go hunting for save_* functions.
Insert vs update is decided by presence of id; an insert must .select('id').single() and RETURN the new uuid so staged child rows (sign-up slots) can be attached right after the first save.

⚠️⚠️ updated_by must come from the CACHED local session, never a network user lookup. getUser() stalling on flaky mobile data hung every fest write — the 'Saving…' button never resolved even though reads worked. It's only an audit stamp; nil is fine, a hang is not.
⚠️ is_private is written and read back but NEVER mapped into the display model — nothing on web reads it. Don't build guest-hiding on it and assume parity; raise it as a decision.
DetailsEditor upserts fest_config on fest_year (exactly one row) and validates endDate >= startDate. Changing the dates reshapes every day picker and the countdown.
Dinner titles auto-default to '{Weekday} Dinner' when blank and a day is picked. 'Houses on crew' is comma-separated free text of FAMILY names.

⚠️ The iOS→web session hand-off already exists: FestPlanner reads #mlr_at=/&mlr_rt= from the URL fragment, calls setSession, and strips the tokens from history, holding a 'Checking access…' state so it doesn't flash a sign-in prompt. If iOS changes how it opens that link it breaks into 'the website says I'm not signed in'.
FEST_YEAR is hardcoded to 2026 in lib/festContent.ts — make it one constant on iOS too, or derive it from fest_config.
features.nativeOpportunity: Handoff from a phone schedule row to the master editor on a Mac; photo picking straight from PHPicker with background URLSession upload so a big cover image doesn't block the sheet.
features.v1Cut: Do NOT port the master (variant="page") editor at all — it exists to break out of the phone column for desktop bulk editing; keep the existing web hand-off. Ship DetailsEditor + DuesSheet + PayeeSheet (three tiny forms) first, then DinnerSheet, then ScheduleSheet last.

features.name: Family Fest RSVP + per-day picker
features.whatItDoes: Say whether you're coming and which days, and see how many people are here each day.
gotchas: Scoped to the SYNTHESIZED event id 'family-fest-2026' — Family Fest is deliberately NOT a row in `events`, so its dates have one source of truth. Attendance keys on a stable string id, not an FK.
⚠️ Going / Can't-make only — NO Maybe (hideMaybe) for fest planning.
⚠️ Renders NOTHING once isLive || isWrap: 'keeping this card around post-start would just be a stale are-you-coming nag during/after the thing you're already at'.
⚠️ Guests cannot read event_attendance at all (the 0081 lockdown), so all counts are zero — show a sign-in nudge, never a false 'No RSVPs yet'.
Once you're going and there is more than one day, the card COLLAPSES to 'You're in for Family Fest ✅' + 'Here Mon, Tue' / 'You're here all week', with Change to re-expand.
No per-day picks recorded means 'here all week', not 'here no days'.
Attendance mechanics themselves belong to the events section — coordinate rather than reimplementing.
features.nativeOpportunity: Confetti + haptics on 'going' (web does this with framer-motion); and an RSVP can offer 'add the week to my calendar' in the same tap.

features.name: Phase-gated shortcuts (dues callout, committee contact)
features.whatItDoes: A 'pay your dues' row appears in the run-up and disappears once the week starts; a 'contact the Family Fest committee' row appears only during the week.
gotchas: FestDuesCallout renders only when isPlanning; FestCommitteesLink only when isLive.
⚠️ BOTH read the lib/data.ts FAMILY_FEST date constant, not fest_config — which is exactly why the dues callout can disagree with the countdown on web. Read fest_config on iOS.
duesSummary() picks the Adult tier if priced, else the first priced tier, else 'Tap to see amounts' — never a bare '$0'.

features.name: Admin-set fest cover photo
features.whatItDoes: The banner across the top of the Family Fest screen, replaceable by an organizer so both apps update together.
gotchas: Three-step fallback, in order: app_images['fest_cover'] → the mini's /assets/site/family-fest-2026.jpg → the bundled asset. Implement all three; the error-swap to the bundled copy is what stops a broken image in the header.

⚠️ /assets is one of the mini's deliberately unauthenticated paths (isAlwaysPublic), so the mini fallback needs no token — but an admin-set cover or an event image_url that resolves to the mini's /f tree DOES.

⚠️⚠️ MEDIA_AUTH on the mini is currently 'report', not 'on', SPECIFICALLY because the native app cannot sign media URLs yet — enforcement would 403 every photo for the 3 registered iOS devices. Ship the token signer before anyone promotes it to 'on'. And never generate a fresh MEDIA_TOKEN_SECRET while testing: the signing key falls back to SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, so setting it for the first time is a KEY ROTATION that 403s every already-issued token.

features.name: "Notify about this change" from the editors
features.whatItDoes: When an organizer moves dinner to 6:00, they can tell everyone at the fest in the same breath — a banner, an Activity entry, an email, or any combination.
rpcs: send_broadcast_notification(p_title, p_body, p_url, p_audience, p_expires_at, p_event_id, p_exclude_not_attending)
gotchas: Mount ONLY when isAdmin && editing an existing item — the underlying broadcast paths are admin-gated server-side.
Defaults: enabled OFF, but banner ON and activity ON, email OFF, so ticking it once does the sensible thing.
Prefilled message via changeMessageDefault: '{title} is now at 6:00 PM', else 'Update: {title}'.
Targeting is always p_event_id='family-fest-2026' + p_exclude_not_attending=true — it hides the notice ONLY from someone who explicitly RSVP'd Can't-make; a no-response member still gets it.
Banner + email share ONE announcements row: show_banner=false with notify_email=true is email-only (no banner, no push).
⚠️ Banner expiry defaults to 3 HOURS — a time-change notice must not still be at the top of the app tomorrow.

⚠️ Send AFTER the save succeeds, and on failure surface 'Saved — but the notification didn't send: …' while BLOCKING the sheet from closing. Never roll back a successful content save because a notification failed.
features.nativeOpportunity: An actionable notification: 'Dinner moved to 6:00' with an inline 'Update my calendar' action, which the web's push cannot offer.

features.name: "See the app as if it's this day"
features.whatItDoes: A hidden setting that pretends today is a different date, so an organizer can look at the live week or the wrap phase before it happens.
gotchas: This is the only practical way to test all four phases without waiting a year — port it or you cannot QA this section.
Anchored at NOON ('{date}T12:00:00') so timezone slop can't shift the simulated day.
With an override set, the countdown goes STATIC rather than ticking.
With no override, web refreshes hourly so a long-open tab rolls over days — the iOS equivalent is the foreground/day-change recompute.
⚠️ Strictly device-local (UserDefaults). It must NEVER reach the server; a demo date leaking into a write would stamp a fake day on a schedule row.

features.name: The parchment / Renaissance look
features.whatItDoes: Family Fest looks and feels like its own place — aged parchment, sepia ink, heraldic wine and azure, and an inscriptional serif — while the rest of the app stays forest green.
gotchas: Exact tokens: background #f4ecd8, foreground #3a2a18, card #fdfaf1, border #d8c7a3, primary #8b2e2e (gules), accent #1e3a8a (azure); display face Cinzel with 0.02em tracking. Outside the section the fest brand color is the separate --color-fest #8b2e2e (tab bar + live dot).
P3 variants exist: primary color(displayP3 0.57 0.15 0.15), accent color(displayP3 0.1 0.22 0.56) — use Color(.displayP3, …) so wide-gamut screens get the richer heraldry.
There is a layered ambient wash, not a flat fill: a wine radial at the top, a sepia vignette at the bottom, over a parchment gradient.

⚠️ FestThemeSync exists because scoping the theme to the CONTENT BOX left the resort's green showing through during rubber-band bounce. The native analogue: paint parchment on the scroll view background AND the navigation bar, not just the content — a green nav bar over parchment content is exactly that bug.
⚠️ LIGHT MODE ONLY, deliberately, app-wide. Do not invent a dark parchment; force .preferredColorScheme(.light) for this subtree instead.
Never hard-code the hexes at call sites — inject a theme, mirroring how the web re-declares variables so utilities pick them up.
features.nativeOpportunity: Real materials (.ultraThinMaterial) behind the sticky sub-nav instead of a faked backdrop-blur; matchedGeometryEffect for the gliding nav pill (web already uses layoutId 'ff-nav-pill'); and the identity can extend to an alternate app icon during the live week.

features.name: Offline-first fest schedule
features.whatItDoes: The whole week — every event, dinner, menu, location, and phone number — works with no signal at all, which is the normal condition five miles out of Tomahawk.
gotchas: iOS-native addition with no web equivalent beyond a best-effort localStorage snapshot (key 'festContent', 24h TTL) — the browser cannot cache the images or guarantee the whole bundle.
Persist to disk in an App Group container so the widget and Live Activity read the SAME cache; render from it unconditionally at launch and revalidate behind it.
Pre-warm during the planning phase with a BGAppRefreshTask so the cache is already full when someone drives up and loses signal.
Show a quiet 'last updated' line, never a blocking spinner. The schedule must never wait on the network.

⚠️ Mirror the web's fallback asymmetry: an EMPTY fest table means fall back to the bundled seed so the screen is never blank; an empty home_callouts means 'no call-outs' and must NOT resurrect a deleted card.

⚠️ Don't rely on Realtime for freshness — no migration adds the six fest content tables to the supabase_realtime publication (only the slots/signups tables), so web's fest subscription may be dead. Verify in the dashboard; foreground refresh + pull-to-refresh is the right design regardless.
⚠️ If you do subscribe, keep home_callouts on its OWN channel — a postgres_changes binding to a nonexistent table fails the entire channel join.
features.nativeOpportunity: This IS the native opportunity: a browser cannot guarantee an offline schedule with cached cover art and every lead's phone number.

features.name: Live Activity + widget for "today at the fest"
features.whatItDoes: On the Lock Screen during the week: Day 3 of 7, and what's next and where. On the Home Screen the rest of the year: a countdown.
gotchas: iOS-native addition; no web counterpart exists or can.
Start the Live Activity when the season phase flips to live, end it at wrap. Drive it from the same merged dayTimeline used on screen so the two can never disagree.
Widget: a TimelineProvider with one entry per item start advances with no refresh budget spent — don't poll.
⚠️ Feed both from the shared App Group cache, never a network call. A widget refresh that fails on bad wifi must show the cached schedule, not 'unable to load'.
During planning, the widget mirrors Countdown (days/hrs/min to startDate); during off-season it should say 'Returns next summer', matching the web's quiet banner.
features.nativeOpportunity: This IS the native opportunity — the single highest-leverage thing iOS can do that the web app structurally cannot.
features.v1Cut: Ship the widget (countdown + today's list) first; the Live Activity is the larger, week-only half.

features.name: Add the fest week to your calendar
features.whatItDoes: One tap puts every event and dinner into a Family Fest calendar on your phone, with locations, what to bring, and reminders — so the OS you already trust nudges you.
gotchas: iOS-native addition. The web's equivalent is a planned ICS feed that was never built — lib/events.ts fetchGcalEvents() still returns [].
Write to a DEDICATED 'Family Fest 2026' EKCalendar so the user can delete it wholesale.
Store the EKEvent identifiers keyed by fest row id so a later schedule change updates the existing event in place rather than duplicating it.
⚠️ Times are FREE TEXT ('18:00' or '6:00 PM' or 'TBD'). Skip or mark all-day anything unparseable; do NOT invent a time.
⚠️ Anytime items have no real day (0141 parked it on current_date) — export them as an all-day event spanning the whole week, or not at all. Never on their parked day.
⚠️ Build every date with an explicit local calendar, never an ISO8601 full-date parse (see the day-early incident).
features.nativeOpportunity: This IS the native opportunity — EventKit is unavailable to a PWA.

features.name: Family Fest card on Home
features.whatItDoes: On the resort home screen, one card that changes with the season: a quiet banner most of the year, 'planning underway', today's whole agenda during the week, and a 'post your photos' nudge after.
gotchas: This card may belong to the Home section's spec — coordinate so it isn't built twice.
During live it shows the WHOLE day inline (every event + tonight's dinner with times, locations and the menu), not a teaser: 'nobody should have to click through just to see what's later today'.

The committee-membership check is cached under the SAME festMember.{uid} key FestStatus uses, so the two share one deduped fetch — otherwise the 'Join the Family Fest committee' CTA flashes in and vanishes for an actual member on every home visit.
A revalidate must be able to flip membership back to false, so a member who left gets the CTA back.
⚠️ Wrap CTA points at the Drop Box Family Fest album, not the Feed — and iOS has no Drop Boxes yet.
It is the permanent, non-swipeable BASE of the Home call-out stack — temporary call-outs stack on top of it and it never goes away.

features.name: Guest / waiting-to-be-approved / member gating
features.whatItDoes: Anyone can browse the app, but private things are hidden until you sign in — and a brand-new signup sees only public content, with a clear explanation, until a family admin okays their account.
gotchas: ⚠️ The DB column is profiles.approved but every human-facing string says "Verified" — Supabase already owns "verified" for email OTP. Do not unify them.

⚠️ approved == nil, a read error, or a missing column MUST resolve to APPROVED. The web defaults verified=true in three places (initial state, error branch, column-absent) because the other default locks real members out over a network blip.
⚠️ An unverified member must NOT be shown a "Sign in" button — they already signed in. Own copy, no button, non-interactive 🔒 chip inline.
⚠️ profiles keeps an own-row escape hatch (is_approved_member() or id = auth.uid()). Without it identity loading breaks for exactly the people who need the waiting screen.

⚠️ An empty array from any members-only table means NOT PERMITTED, not "no data". Never render an empty-state that implies emptiness on those surfaces — web degrades them to sign-in nudges (EventSheet "Sign in to see who's coming", WorkChecklist "Sign in to see the resort to-do list").
⚠️ Public-read regardless of session: events, cabins, announcements, committees, committee_areas, app_images, fest_content tables, resort_config. Empty there really is empty.
⚠️ The client is not the enforcement boundary — this is a Supabase-token app and anyone can hit the REST API with their own JWT. The wall exists to make the screen coherent.
⚠️ Guests see first names only (firstName(): name.trim().split(/\s+/)[0]), fed by the public_profiles view server-side. Don't render a full name a guest fetched from a fallback path.
⚠️ Admin "view as" forces verified: true and needsIntro: false — an admin checking the guest view must not appear unverified to themselves.
features.nativeOpportunity: The web needs a `resolving` skeleton state because prerendered HTML always ships the guest view, so a returning member can flash the sign-in wall on every cold open. iOS restores the session from the Keychain synchronously, so the very first frame can already be the member layout — keep the state for the network `approved` read, but it should be invisible in practice.

features.name: Stay signed in, and open already showing your stuff
features.whatItDoes: A returning member never sees the signed-out version of the app while it loads — their name, avatar and admin tools are there on the first frame.
gotchas: The web snapshots { user, isAdmin } to `identity.<uid>` with an INFINITE TTL (a live session implies the snapshot's owner) and restores it before the network profile fetch.
⚠️ The snapshot deliberately EXCLUDES the one-time intro flags (intro_seen / invitedViaLink) — restoring those could re-show the onboarding sheet.
⚠️ It is one-shot guarded (snapshotSeededRef) so a later auth-state-change re-entry can never clobber fresher state with the stale snapshot.
Accepted trade-off, written down: a since-demoted admin can paint admin UI for ~1s until the fresh profile lands. Fine, because is_admin is UI-only and RLS is the real gate.

⚠️ updateUser() is optimistic AND rolls back on a failed write, re-pinning the snapshot to the last-good value — otherwise a name that only ever lived on-device silently reverts to the email-prefix default on the next cold load.

Profile column mapping for writes: name→display_name, emailAlerts→email_alerts, pushTypes→push_types, pushSelfNotify→push_self_notify, notifyNewMembers→notify_new_members, notifTypes→notif_types, pushPrompted→push_prompted, willingToHelp→willing_to_help, avatarUrl→avatar_url.
Email change is in-app, two calls: auth.updateUser({ email }) then auth.verifyOtp({ email, token, type: "email_change" }). profiles stores no email, so nothing else needs syncing.

Sign-in: signInWithOtp({ email, options: { shouldCreateUser: true } }) then verifyOtp({ email, token, type: "email" }). ⚠️ The code field accepts 6–8 digits on purpose — never hard-code 6, since the project's OTP length can be reconfigured. 30s resend cooldown so tap-tap-tap can't trip Supabase's rate limit.
features.nativeOpportunity: Keychain-backed session restore is synchronous and survives app reinstall-adjacent cases better than localStorage; combined with a synchronous disk cache read, the first frame is the real member view with zero flash. Also: no Safari-vs-installed-PWA split login, so nobody ever signs in twice.

features.name: Tapping a notification lands on the exact thing
features.whatItDoes: Tapping "Cass commented on your post" opens that post at that comment — not the top of the feed.
gotchas: The full path inventory the triggers actually emit: /posts?post=<id>, /posts?post=<id>&comment=<id>, /posts?c=<slug>&m=<id>[&area=<area>], /posts?house=<slug>&m=<id>, /posts?c=<slug>[&area=]&poll=<id>, /posts?feed=main, /?work=<id>, /events?open=<id>, /events?activity=<id>, /events?meeting=<id>, /house/calendar?house=<slug>, /people?member=<id>, /family-fest/schedule/<id>, /drop?box=<id>, /request-stay, /admin/cabins?booking=<id>, /admin/committees?committee=<slug>.
⚠️ /chat?m=<id> is LEGACY (migration 0030, superseded by 0063). Older notification rows still carry it — handle it as an alias.

⚠️⚠️ Never route to /committees/<slug>/chat. In the installed PWA that navigation dies before React runs (WebKit's own "This page couldn't load"), while the same room via the Feed works. Every server-side check comes back healthy, so it's invisible outside a real installed PWA; three fixes failed before the cause was found. Even on native, the URL contract matters: the database's notification rows use the /posts?c=… form.
⚠️ Honour &from=<slug> — it's the Back target so a deep-linked room returns to the committee page instead of the chats list.

⚠️ A deep-linked launch must never paint the chats-list state first. Web captures bootChannelKey/bootHouseSlug at mount and holds a "Loading…" instead, because otherwise a member who IS in a house/committee sees the list for a beat and gets visibly "hopped".

⚠️ Queue a cold-launch link and replay it after the viewer state settles. The web's whole PushDeepLink component exists because the SW's client.navigate() rejects in an installed PWA, the error was swallowed, and taps just focused the app on whatever page it already showed.
⚠️ Resolve the link against your own origin and drop anything cross-origin — both sw.js and PushDeepLink filter same-origin before routing.
features.nativeOpportunity: One DeepLink enum with an `init?(path:)` serves cold launch, foreground tap, Universal Link, and in-app navigation. Then: actionable notifications (On my way / RSVP Going / Approve) straight from the lock screen against RPCs that already exist; NSUserActivity for Handoff + Spotlight; App Intents so the same enum powers Shortcuts; Universal Links so shared /drop?box= and /posts?post= links open the app instead of Safari.

features.name: Scroll to and highlight the item you were sent to
features.whatItDoes: After a deep link opens a screen, the specific post, comment or message briefly glows so you can see which one it meant.
gotchas: useDeepLinkFlash(idPrefix, target, ready) polls document.getElementById every 150ms up to 20 attempts (~3s), then scrollIntoView({ block: "center" }), then clears the flash after 2200ms.

⚠️ The polling exists because the target may not be in the DOM yet — a long list still rendering, or a TRIMMED cold-open snapshot that doesn't contain an older item the full fetch hasn't landed yet. Handle "the id isn't in the data" by landing on the screen, never nowhere.

The first landing in a mount snaps (behavior: "auto") because the viewer has nothing to scroll from; a LATER deep link in the same mount scrolls smoothly, because there the motion is the useful cue. Keep both behaviours.
`ready` must be the real data-loaded flag, not some unrelated local-state-settled flag.
PostsView runs TWO independent instances side by side ("post-" and "comment-"); the hook holds no shared state.
features.nativeOpportunity: ScrollViewReader.scrollTo(id, anchor: .center) after awaiting the fetch removes the 3-second DOM poll and the race entirely. The highlight becomes a real animated ring plus a UIImpactFeedbackGenerator tap — a "here it is" cue the web cannot produce.

features.name: Screens paint instantly with the last known data
features.whatItDoes: Opening a tab (or the whole app) shows what you saw last time immediately and quietly refreshes behind it, instead of a spinner and cards popping in.
features.v1Cut: Memory + disk layers honouring rules 2–4 (uid-scoped keys, preview never persists, wipe on sign-out) with a single default TTL and no per-call tuning. Skip: session-vs-local distinction, snapshot trimming heuristics, and the readiness registry integration.
gotchas: Exact surface: useCachedResource(key: string|null, empty, fetcher, { persist?: "local"|"session", ttlMs? }) → { data, loading, reload, mutate }. Prefix "mlr.cache.v1.", MAX_PERSIST_BYTES 200_000, DEFAULT_TTL_MS 24h, envelope { ts, data }.

⛔ RULE 1 IS WEB-ONLY: "memory seeds sync, storage seeds post-mount" exists purely for React hydration (prerendered HTML is always the guest view). iOS should read the disk snapshot SYNCHRONOUSLY before the first frame — strictly better, and it's the property the rule was trying to protect.

⚠️ RULE 2 — user-scoped keys embed the auth uid: identity.<uid>, myHouse.<uid>, feed.<uid>, events.<uid|guest>, unread.<uid>, notifFeed.<uid>, postsFeed.<uid>, people.<uid>, polls.<uid>, activePoll.<uid>, calloutsDone.<uid>, workChecklist.<uid|guest>, helpRequests.<uid>, festMember.<uid>, dropBoxes.<uid>, dropBox.<uid>.<boxId>, privateActivities.<uid>, tournament.<uid>.<hostId>, chatRoom.<uid>.<slug>|<area>, houseChatRoom.<uid>.<slug>, chatPolls.<uid>.<roomKey>, meetings.<uid>.<roomKey>, resolvedHouse.<uid>.<slug|mine>.<isAdmin>, chatEntry.<uid>.<slug>, managedCommittee.<uid>.<slug>.<isAdmin>, houseCalendar.<houseId>, houseLists.<houseId>. Public/unscoped: festContent, appImages, weather.
⚠️ Pass key = nil while the uid is unresolved so the loader is fully INERT — otherwise another account's rows can seed the current viewer's screen.

⚠️ Day-fresh keys embed the LOCAL date (whosUpNorth.<uid>.<date>, birthdays.<uid>.<date>, onThisDay.<uid>.<date>) so a stale day never paints. Compute it from Calendar.current components, never an ISO8601 UTC formatter.

⚠️ RULE 3 — preview mode never persists: pass no persistence AND put the preview id in the memory-only key (myHouse.preview.<id>, activePoll.preview.<id>, chatEntry.preview.<id>.<slug>, resolvedHouse.preview.…). A leaked preview snapshot paints the previewed member's data as the admin's own on the next cold open.

⚠️ RULE 4 — sign-out wipes every mlr.cache.* key in both storages plus the memory and in-flight maps, and separately clears the media token. Uid-scoped keys are the backstop for the token-expiry path where sign-out never runs.

⚠️ Device preferences deliberately SURVIVE sign-out and must not be lumped in: mlr-text-scale, mlr-welcomed, mlr-dismissed-announcements, mlr.callouts.dismissed, mlr.callouts.wiggled, mlr.installNudge.seen, mlr.dropbox.sort, mlr.flaggedPosts, mlr-demo-date.

⚠️ Two entries are TRIMMED snapshots because of the 200KB cap: postsFeed.<uid> is the top ~15 posts with their comments/reactions/members, and chatRoom/houseChatRoom keep the last ~30 messages plus access/roster. Never persist full history — and keep some cap on iOS or a big album turns launch into a multi-MB main-thread decode.

⚠️ Caching chat messages on disk was an owner-approved trade-off (the member can already read the room), uid-scoped and wiped on sign-out. Do not extend that reasoning to anything the viewer can't already read.
loading is true ONLY when nothing seeded; a warm seed serves stale with loading=false. A rejected fetch must never stick on loading — clear it and keep the stale data.
⚠️ Commit the fetched value to the cache even when the view is gone / the task was cancelled ("cache even if unmounted — don't lose the fetch"), then check cancellation before publishing state.
In-flight requests are deduped per key so two screens mounting the same key share one round-trip; reload() REPLACES a stale in-flight entry rather than joining it.
Everything is stale-while-revalidate: a seed ALWAYS gets a background refetch, which is how revoked access and deleted rows self-correct.
features.nativeOpportunity: No 200KB quota and no synchronous localStorage: the snapshot can be the whole feed, decoded off the main actor into Application Support (not Caches/, which iOS purges). URLCache handles media for free — and because /f accepts `Authorization: Bearer <mediaToken>` as well as ?t=, iOS can keep cache keys clean and keep the token out of URLs and logs. Combined, that gives genuine offline reads at a lake with no signal, which the web app cannot do at all (its service worker deliberately caches nothing).

features.name: Hold the launch screen until the first screen is actually complete
features.whatItDoes: The app doesn't reveal a half-empty Home and then pop cards in — it waits (briefly, with a hard ceiling) for the first screen's data.
features.v1Cut: Ship a plain launch screen with no readiness gate at all; add the registry once the cache layer exists (on a warm open the gate adds ~0ms anyway, so it only pays off on first launch).
gotchas: markPending(key) fires ONLY on a cold load (nothing seeded), and the returned done() is idempotent and also called on unmount.
Constants: HOLD_MS 1300 minimum hold, EXTRA_QUIET_MS 700 extra wait for cold loads, MAX_WAIT_MS 4500 which ALWAYS wins, FLY_MS 720.

⚠️ onQuietOnce defers its first "already quiet?" check by a microtask so loads registered in the same commit are counted. Without that the gate concludes quiet before anything registered and does nothing. In Swift: one Task.yield() / run-loop hop before the first check.
⚠️ Every path out of the hold must be bounded. Web has TWO independent nets: the JS MAX_WAIT_MS timer and a pure-CSS splash-wash animation that clears the overlay even if JS never runs.

⛔ Do not port the FLIP logo fly (measure #app-logo, translate/scale onto it, hold the header copy at opacity 0 via html[data-splash]). That whole mechanism exists because the web has no launch screen.
Reduce-motion must skip straight to the app — web checks prefers-reduced-motion in three separate places for this.

A "bare route" concept exists (lib/bareRoutes.ts = ["/family-fest/master"]) so the fest master editor opened FROM the iOS app drops straight in with no splash or install nag. Keep passing that route if iOS still opens that editor in a web view.
features.nativeOpportunity: iOS can hold the real system launch screen rather than painting a fake overlay over the app, and matchedGeometryEffect gives the "logo placed into the header" effect without measuring anything.

features.name: First-run welcome (notifications, then your basics)
features.whatItDoes: The first time a new member signs in, a short guided sheet turns on notifications and collects phone, birthday and how they like to be paid, so they never have to find Settings.
gotchas: Gate: needsIntro = !intro_seen && (!phone?.trim() && !birthday && !pay_preferred). Computed in a SEPARATE, try/catch-guarded query so a pre-migration column can never break sign-in.
⚠️ Push comes FIRST, basics second — deliberate, so the first thing after verifying is "turn on notifications", not a form.

It mounts the REAL PushToggle settings (master on by default, untick what you don't want), not a fake preview. Reaching that step stamps profiles.push_prompted so the standalone PushPrompt never asks twice — web skips the stamp on iOS-before-install; native should always stamp it.
The basics step writes TWO columns for pay: row[payMethod] = handle plus row.pay_preferred = payMethod, where payMethod ∈ venmo|zelle|cashapp|paypal.

⚠️ AWAIT the display-name write before navigating away. An unawaited write was cut off mid-flight and rolled the new member back to the email-prefix default name (motu42). try await, never a detached Task.

⚠️ Dismissing (✕/backdrop) counts as finishing the current step so it never re-nags, and the sheet hides on a LOCAL flag independent of the network write — otherwise a slow completeIntro() strands a dimmed overlay over the app.
completeIntro() clears the flag locally first, then persists intro_seen inside a try/catch (no-op pre-migration).
It deliberately SUPERSEDES the standalone PushPrompt, which holds off while needsIntro is true.
features.nativeOpportunity: The push step becomes a real UNUserNotificationCenter.requestAuthorization at the exact moment the person wants notifications — far better conversion than a web push dialog, and with no "add to home screen first" caveat to explain. Birthday gets a native DatePicker wheel instead of the hand-rolled BirthdayPicker; the phone field gets .phonePad + formatting; the pay handle can offer paste detection.

features.name: "Is this you?" check on an admin invite link
features.whatItDoes: An admin's invite email signs in whoever taps it, so before letting them in the app asks them to type the address it was sent to — a forwarded invite can't quietly land someone in another member's account.
gotchas: Driven by profiles.invited_via = 'invite_link' AND needsIntro still true (one-time, clears with the intro).
⚠️ The step NEVER displays the target email — typing it blind is what verifies it's theirs; glancing at a displayed address and tapping Continue verifies nothing.
⚠️ After 3 wrong attempts it signs the person out rather than ever revealing whose account it almost was.
⚠️ The confirm step has NO close button and gets no step-indicator dot — dismissing must not be a silent way to end up inside the account without confirming or signing out.
Comparison is trim + lowercase on both sides.

features.name: Signing out leaves nothing behind
features.whatItDoes: When someone signs out on a shared iPad or a borrowed phone, none of their feed, chats, photos or name can paint for the next person.
gotchas: signOut() does FOUR things: auth.signOut(), clearAllCaches() (memory map + in-flight map + every mlr.cache.* key in BOTH storages), clearMediaToken(), and clears the preview key + all identity state.

⚠️ Uid-scoped keys are the SECOND line of defence for the token-expiry path where signOut never runs — leftover entries are inert without a session. Both layers are needed; neither alone is sufficient.
⚠️ Do NOT wipe the device-preference keys (text size, welcome-card seen, dismissed announcements, dropbox sort…). They belong to the device, not the account.

There is a real recorded incident behind this: a cache keyed on a shared "self" string instead of the real user identity leaked one member's cached private chat to the next user, because signOut doesn't reload the page. Key user-specific caches on the actual uid, always.
features.nativeOpportunity: Keychain deletion plus a directory removal is atomic and verifiable in a way clearing localStorage key-by-key is not; you can assert the cache directory is empty in a test.

features.name: Admin "view as" never contaminates the admin's own data
features.whatItDoes: An admin can look at the app as a specific member or as a guest to check what's private — and nothing they see while previewing gets saved as their own.
gotchas: ⚠️ "Is this MINE?" always resolves through effectiveUserId (= previewAsId ?? userId). Never a raw session lookup and never userId alone — both hand back the real admin during a preview, leaking the admin's Edit/Delete affordances onto the previewed member's screen.
⚠️ Every WRITE must no-op while previewing. View-as is strictly read-only: it never acts as the previewed member, and never as the real admin dressed up as them.

⚠️ The cache key must carry the preview id AND persistence must be off (myHouse.preview.<id> with no disk write). A persisted preview snapshot paints the previewed member's data as the admin's own on their next cold open.
Preview forces isAdmin false, needsIntro false and verified true while active.
Only a "guest" preview is restored across reloads; a specific-member preview needs the in-memory member object and is dropped rather than half-restored.
Preview is UI-only and never touches the real Supabase session, so RLS is unchanged — which is exactly why the client-side rules above are the only thing protecting the data.

features.name: The five bottom tabs
features.whatItDoes: Home, Feed, Family Fest, Activity, Profile — the app's permanent bottom bar.
gotchas: The TABS array is the single source of truth: / Home (home), /posts Feed (feed), /family-fest Family Fest (fest/tent), /notifications Activity (bell), /profile Profile (person).
Active detection: exact match for "/", startsWith for everything else.
⚠️ People is deliberately NOT a tab (it's a Home tile) and Profile IS the last tab (it moved back from a header avatar). Both have been moved before — don't "improve" the arrangement without asking.
⚠️ The Family Fest tab wears --color-fest (#8b2e2e heraldic wine), not forest green, so the fest reads as its own theme from anywhere.
The bar renders no emoji — it's a hand-rolled SVG line-icon set.

⛔ Web-only inside this component: the visualViewport keyboard hide (fixed bottom bars get stranded mid-screen on iOS), an opaque background instead of backdrop-blur (WebKit samples a fixed blurred layer at a stale scroll offset), and translate-y-0 to force a stable compositor layer. None of it transfers.

⚠️ Recorded bug worth knowing: iOS fires a visualViewport resize with WRONG dimensions during background→foreground, which locked the bar off-screen — hence the visibilitychange reset plus a 300ms re-check. If the native app ever measures the keyboard itself, expect the same lie.
features.nativeOpportunity: A native TabView gets the keyboard, safe area, blur material and scroll-to-top-on-retap for free, plus SF Symbols with proper Dynamic Type scaling.

features.name: Unread Activity badge and the live Family Fest dot
features.whatItDoes: A red count on the Activity tab shows how many new things involve you; during fest week the Family Fest tab gets a pulsing live dot.
gotchas: Unread = unseen AND unexpired: notifications.seen_at drives the badge, read_at drives per-item bold, expires_at drops an item from the badge while keeping it in the list. Cache key unread.<uid>.
Counts over 99 render as "99+".
The live dot shows when getFestSeason(start, end) is isLive || isWrap — a pure function over FAMILY_FEST.startDate/.endDate in lib/data.ts, mirrored byte-for-byte in the family-fest repo.

⚠️ The web hook returns null until mounted, because a build-time new Date() would freeze the phase at deploy. On iOS compute it at launch AND on scenePhase .active, or the phase goes stale in a long-lived process.
⚠️ Season dates come from code (lib/data.ts), not a table — so iOS must carry the same constants or read them from wherever the shared source lands. Verify which in the iOS repo.
features.nativeOpportunity: The same unread count sets the app icon badge via UNUserNotificationCenter — the web can't badge a home-screen icon at all. The fest countdown/live state is also an obvious WidgetKit widget and a Live Activity candidate during the event week.

features.name: Bigger text for older eyes
features.whatItDoes: Anyone can make every bit of text in the app larger without breaking the layout.
gotchas: ⛔ The three-button control itself is web-only-by-design: it exists ONLY because the browser has no access to the OS text-size setting. iOS must use Dynamic Type (.font(.body), @ScaledMetric, UIFontMetrics) and honour the size the person already chose in Settings.
Web mechanics for reference: localStorage "mlr-text-scale" ∈ normal|large|largest → 17/19/21px on the html rem root, re-applied pre-paint by a blocking inline script in layout.tsx.
⚠️ globals.css warns: don't re-pin a px font-size on body/html or the whole scaling mechanism breaks. The native analogue is hardcoding .system(size:) instead of a text style.
⚠️ Dynamic Type goes far past the web's 21px ceiling. Audit every card, chip, tab label and member name at AX5, and prefer ViewThatFits/wrapping over truncation.

⚠️ The readability floor is a product rule, not styling: --color-muted #4b5b52 and --color-faint #64716a exist because text-foreground/40 reads too faint for older eyes, and ~40 components were swept onto them. NEVER express secondary text as an opacity on the foreground colour — make them real semantic colours with their own dark values.

⚠️ Doc drift to verify: CLAUDE.md says pinch-zoom is allowed (userScalable: true) but app/layout.tsx currently ships maximumScale: 1, userScalable: false with a comment that stray pinches were zooming the layout. The code is authoritative; the intent is that text scaling — not zoom — is the supported path.
features.nativeOpportunity: Dynamic Type is strictly better than a 3-step custom control: it respects a system-wide preference the person already set, reaches the accessibility sizes the 21px cap can't, and works with VoiceOver, Bold Text and Increase Contrast at the same time.

features.name: The app's colours and (new for iOS) a dark appearance
features.whatItDoes: One forest-green Northwoods palette everywhere, and on iPhone it also has to look right in dark mode.
gotchas: ⚠️⚠️ The web app is LIGHT MODE ONLY by hard rule, stated three times in globals.css plus color-scheme: light. So iOS's dark mode has NO web reference to copy — budget for designing it rather than discovering it at review.

Palette to build the Color set from: background #f6f6f1, foreground #14241c, card #ffffff, border #e5e4da, primary #15503a, logo #0c4029, accent #c2410c, lake #0e7490, campfire #c2410c, sun #b45309, dusk #6d28d9, fest #8b2e2e, muted #4b5b52, faint #64716a, venmo #3d95ce, paypal #003087.

⚠️ NEVER use a dark translucent tint (bg-black/NN, bg-zinc/NN) as a card or panel background — it goes muddy grey on light. Recurring bug across this author's apps. A dark wash is fine ONLY as a modal scrim. In dark mode this rule INVERTS (a thin dark material over a dark ground is correct), so decide per-surface rather than porting the rule literally.

There is a Display-P3 layer that enriches only the ACCENTS (primary, accent, lake, campfire, sun, dusk, fest) while background, foreground, cards, borders, the readability floors and the logo band stay sRGB — because the logo band must match the raster logo exactly. Mirror that split in the asset catalogue (P3 accents, sRGB neutrals).
⚠️ --color-logo #0c4029 is the exact green baked into the raster logo image; the Home header band uses it so the shrunken logo blends seamlessly. Don't substitute --color-primary there.
Never hard-code a colour in a view — add or edit a token/semantic colour.
features.nativeOpportunity: Asset-catalogue colours give per-appearance and per-gamut variants natively, so the P3 accents render properly on every modern iPhone with an sRGB fallback — a cleaner version of what the web fakes with an @supports block.

features.name: Family Fest looks like its own place inside the app
features.whatItDoes: The Family Fest section swaps to a parchment-and-wine Renaissance look while the rest of the resort app stays forest green.
gotchas: Web scopes it by re-declaring the SAME --color-* variables under .ff-section: background #f4ecd8, foreground #3a2a18, card #fdfaf1, border #d8c7a3, primary #8b2e2e (heraldic wine), accent #1e3a8a (azure), plus a Cinzel display serif for h1/.font-display.
⚠️ Outside the fest section the wine is --color-fest, a separate token — that's what the Family Fest tab and its live dot use.

Web needs TWO extra hacks that don't transfer: html[data-ff] (toggled by FestThemeSync) so the viewport canvas behind rubber-band bounce matches, and Sheet/ModalPortal re-applying .ff-section by route because portaling to <body> escapes the subtree.

⚠️ On iOS this is an @Environment theme value injected at the Family Fest tab root; sheets inherit it through the environment, so the re-application problem simply doesn't exist. Don't port the class-toggling.
⚠️ The parchment theme also needs a dark counterpart with no web reference — think candle-lit vellum, not an inverted parchment.
features.nativeOpportunity: An environment-injected Theme struct means a fest sheet, alert or share preview is themed automatically, and the transition between resort and fest chrome can animate rather than snap.

features.name: Coming back to the app shows current information
features.whatItDoes: Reopening the app after it's been in the background quietly refreshes what changed instead of showing yesterday's feed.
gotchas: Web hooks four separate signals for this: visibilitychange, window focus, pageshow.persisted (a PWA restored from the back/forward cache), and a 5-minute interval.
⚠️ On iOS this all collapses to @Environment(\.scenePhase) == .active — and that is also the right place to re-run the media-token reconcile.

⚠️⚠️ The media token MUST be refetched on every app open (force), cached or not. A cached token is only a guess about what the server will accept; when the server's signing key changed, clients kept confidently signing URLs with a dead key and every photo 403'd for up to 24h with NO self-healing. That is a real outage that happened the day enforcement went on.

⚠️ Obtaining a token must also force a re-render of anything already painted. On web, mediaSrc() reads the token synchronously during render and returns the URL UNSIGNED when there isn't one — so a bare fire-and-forget warm left every already-painted image unsigned forever. The Swift analogue: publish the token and let AsyncImage/URLRequest builders observe it.
Realtime subscriptions are the other half of freshness and are per-feature; this item is only the app-level tick.
features.nativeOpportunity: scenePhase is a single, reliable signal where the web needs four unreliable ones (and one of them, pageshow.persisted, exists purely to paper over PWA back/forward-cache restores). BGAppRefreshTask can additionally warm the cache before the person even opens the app, so the first frame is already current.

features.name: "A new version is available" nudge
features.whatItDoes: Tells someone their app is running an old build and offers a one-tap refresh.
gotchas: ⛔ Web-only-by-design: it exists because an installed iOS PWA keeps running the build it launched with until fully closed and reopened. The App Store solves this. Same for ChunkErrorRecovery, which catches ChunkLoadError from a session still on an old bundle and does one guarded hard reload (mlr.chunkRecovery.lastReload, one attempt per 30s) — a bundler problem with no native analogue.
For reference: NEXT_PUBLIC_BUILD_ID is baked into the bundle and published at /version.json from one source in next.config.ts so they can't disagree; the banner polls no-store with a cache-buster.

⚠️ Refresh purges all of Cache Storage and calls registration.update() but deliberately does NOT unregister the service worker — that would drop the push subscription. If iOS ever adds a "reset the app" affordance, keep the same instinct: never clear the thing that holds the push registration.

⚠️ There is NO minimum-version signal in the database today. A native "please update" gate WOULD need a backend change. Recommendation: skip it for v1 — every client seam already degrades gracefully on a missing table/column (42P01 / column-not-found retries). If it's later wanted, add one column to resort_config (already a public-read singleton, already admin-writable) rather than a new table.
features.nativeOpportunity: The real native equivalent isn't a stale bundle, it's stale data — covered by scenePhase refresh and BGAppRefreshTask. A passive "What's new" screen keyed on the local build number covers the rest with no server support.

features.name: The app still works with no signal at the lake
features.whatItDoes: With bad or no reception, the schedule, feed, chats and already-seen photos are still readable instead of the app being blank.
features.v1Cut: Read-only offline: serve the existing disk snapshots and URLCache'd media, show a quiet "showing saved copy" note, and require connectivity for every write. Skip queued/offline writes entirely — they'd need conflict handling across 20+ RPCs.
gotchas: The web app CANNOT do this: sw.js deliberately handles only push and notificationclick with no fetch/caching handler, so nothing is available offline. There is no web behaviour to copy — this is net-new and native-only.

⚠️ Media caching depends on the token: because the token is stable for its whole 24h window, the same photo URL is byte-identical across renders and caches properly. Sending the token as an Authorization header (which /f accepts) keeps URLCache keys clean and makes the cached entry survive a token rotation.

⚠️ Don't cache anything the viewer might lose access to and present it as current — everything is stale-while-revalidate for a reason (revoked committee access, deleted rows and moderation holds self-correct on the refetch).
⚠️ Held/removed content: a row's moderation status can flip to 'pending' AFTER it was cached, because moderation is asynchronous. Re-read status on revalidate and honour it when rendering.
features.nativeOpportunity: This is the single clearest place iOS can be flatly better than the browser, and it matches the actual physical situation — a resort near Tomahawk, WI with patchy signal. Disk snapshots + URLCache + AVAssetDownload for a video someone wants to keep.

features.name: Taps and transitions that feel physical
features.whatItDoes: Buttons, tab taps, sends and confirmations give a small physical response, and animations respect the person's reduce-motion setting.
gotchas: ⚠️ lib/haptics.ts is Android-only and an explicit NO-OP on iOS. So every haptic the web app asked for — including the tab-tap one wired into TabBar — has never once fired for an iPhone user. Everything here is unclaimed ground.

Reduce-motion is honoured in three ways web-side: a global MotionProvider with reducedMotion="user", a media query that collapses every animation to a 1ms fade, and explicit checks before the splash fly, the callout wiggle and every sheet dismiss. Mirror all three intents with @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion).

The motion vocabulary worth matching: page push (a short right-to-left slide, deliberately starting at 0.55 opacity so the screen can never blink), sheet slide-up, centred pop for modals, a spring press-release on tap, a spring pop on the active tab icon, and a hold-then-fade cover when a chat room opens.

⚠️ The chat-open cover (chat-unmask) exists to hide a message list painting/reflowing under a slide-in. On iOS a NavigationStack push with pre-loaded data has nothing to mask — don't port the cover, port the requirement (never reveal a room mid-layout).
features.nativeOpportunity: CoreHaptics / UIImpactFeedbackGenerator gives what lib/haptics.ts was written for and could never deliver on iPhone: a light tap on tab change and reaction, a success notification on RSVP/vote/send, a warning on a held-for-review post. Pair it with the deep-link flash so "here's the thing you tapped" is felt as well as seen.

features.name: Uploads that keep going when you put the phone away
features.whatItDoes: Pick 30 photos, lock the phone or switch apps, and the upload finishes anyway instead of dying.
rpcs: add_drop_box_media(p_box, p_url, p_type, p_thumbnail_url, p_captured_at, p_captured_at_source, p_credit_user_id)
gotchas: ⚠️ A background URLSession CANNOT use an in-memory body — write the multipart body to a file and use uploadTask(with:fromFile:). Foreground works, background silently never fires.
